poem:
I'm hurting,
But no one notices.
I'm bleeding,
But nobody cares.

The pain is too much,
I can't take it anymore.
I want to scream,
And beg for help.

But is there someone,
Even just one,
Who will lend an ear,
To my agonizing cries?

I'm fighting my battle alone,
Treading plight on my own.
Tears is my only solace,
And darkness is my safe place.

I'm down, crippled;
Almost crawling to the ground.
What will happen in the coming days?
When will this misery end?

You're words are sharp.
So sharp like knife.
You're not even aware
you're hurting me deep.
And slowly
breaking my heart
into pieces.

But like the moon
glowing at night,
you see
the radiance of my smile
as if I'm okay.
My mouth is zipped.
No words from me.
You paint the town red
with your lies and scheme.
But I remain calm.
Still like the river.
Even deep inside me
I want to roar like a lion
and hiss like a snake.

If I stoop on your level,
what benefits will I get?
Nothing good right?
So I'll better be quiet
and let you do
what makes you happy.
I believe in due time
you will meet karma.

Don’t judge me by what you see,
I’m not what you expect me to be.
But if you take the time to know me,
You’ll find there’s so much more to see.

Don’t judge me by what you hear,
Don't believe in rumors everywhere.
Step in close, please lend an ear —
You'll hear the truth loud and clear.

Look beyond, not just the surface shown,
Dig deeper — explore my world within
Touch my heart and feel my silent fight,
Wear my soul to see beyond your sight.

Since I was a child,
I dreamed of climbing
the highest peak,
so I tried and tried.

I gave my best,
I did what I could
to reach the top,
but it wasn't that easy.

Years have gone by,
but I am still here,
still struggling to climb
the mountain up high.

There were times
when I felt tired;
every step seemed too heavy—
I thought I was losing energy.

My heart bleeds in silence,
and my tears kiss the night,
but my dream doesn't fade,
and I refuse to let go.

Every time I fall,
I rise again
with hope in my heart—
one day I'll reach the top.

I look okay,
You see me smile each day.
My aura, as radiant as the sun!
I walk with confidence,
But I bleed in silence.

I look brave,
Tough like a warrior;
But deep inside I'm shaking.
I'm but a child,
Fragile and helpless.

I laugh with everyone,
Like nothing is wrong.
My voice is the loudest,
But when I'm alone,
I allow myself to be me.

Life is hard but I'm hoping,
When I wake up one morning,
These silent struggles,
And the wounds I keep hidden,
Will slowly disappear.

I wonder what's behind this wall?
What does it look in the outside world?
Is it safe out there, is it beautiful
Or is it really dangerous?

All my life I'm like a caged bird.
I'm not allowed to spread my wings,
And fly freely in the vast blue sky.
I'm forbidden to go outside.

They say it is better to stay inside.
They say it is better to hide;
Because people will not understand,
Because people will laugh.

All I want is to see,
What's beyond that wall.
Why I can't walk or run like they do?
Ah, I really don't know!

Confusion is flooding my head.
So many questions,
But there are no answers.
I swear curiosity is killing me.

The places we went still hold our fun WHY WONT YOU LEAVE ME ALONE

The secrets we locked away came crashing through WHY WONT YOU LEAVE ME ALONE
The child in me has not left WHY WONT YOU LEAVE ME ALONE
IT'S TIME TO GO SO LEAVE ME ALONE

There is no light only darkness.....I can't see through this haze of despair......feels like I'm
suffocating on my own fears......drowning in the sea of my own mind.....can't feel love or joy
it's banished from my soul....endless nights alone in the dark wondering what happened to
me.......I use to have fun I use to smile I use to laugh and I use to love ....... now all I do is
stay in the dark hidden in the shadows creeping slowly to nothingness......how far can I go
before I find my way back...if I find it at all..... noone can see the pain noone can feel my
broken spirit noone can touch my bleeding heart noone can find the real me....its cold and

Every aggressive word clenches deep in my gut
Every yell at me breaks a piece off my soul
Every shouted sentence steals a piece of me
Every neglect pushes me away
Every forgotten memory ices my veins
Every unheard word shatters my heart
Every ignored cry leaves me bleeding from inside
Every tear shed alone crushes my body
Every unanswered question leaves me empty
Every lie you say breaks your vow
Why do you leave me so cold wishing for warmth that once was there??

Away across the fields
The clouds come down
And dip the trees in mist.
Paler as the distance goes,
Like a child's painting but
Unfinished without the blue sky
And the wobbly round sun.
My mind’s eye adds them there
In impossible colours,
Using crayons and felt-tip pens.
An unreliable arrangement –
The sun was never over those trees.
A passing thought,
Not worth putting up on the fridge.
The shrouded view is here, now.
Beautiful in its own way, and
Indifferent to my views,
Or how I might wish it to be.
Tomorrow it will look differently.
Perhaps tomorrow I will be somewhere else,
And the view more inspiring –
Worth keeping in a box up in the attic.

As a poet who’s often found writing rhyme
I feel, sometimes, that I’m stuck in the slime.
On the banks of a primeval swamp –
Neither lizard nor leopard, just a wallowing lump.
I dimly perceive I could be something more
If I roll up my sleeves and evolve.
But part of me likes the mulchy morass:
I’m a lump with a problem to solve.
In the distance I hear wild poets declaim,
Lambasting me – “Take action!”
“Stop flopping about and grow some legs –
Join the non-rhyming faction.”
Trapped by the rhyme and lacking a spine
Stymied by soft, sucking mud.
Despite lofty aims and lumpy remains,
Rhyming runs deep in my blood.

The crows have gathered
And are having a chat.
They're not plotting murder,
As a matter of fact –
A crow, while unlikely
To do anyone in,
Will happily crow about
Poisoning your gin.
Zebra’s get together,
But not in a herd.
Chit-chatting at checkouts
About gossip they've heard.
They confuse the scanners
With their zeal for a bargain,
And they earned their stripes
By sticking the knife in.
The judicial shrews
Are clutching their pearls
As hyenas cackle at
The gossiping girls.
A shrewd observer would
See their furs were fake,
And the circling vultures
Who’re here for your wake.

“I hope you’ve had a good night’s sleep”
I blink blurry eyes, my face in a heap –
Inside my head I’m still counting sheep.
“What kind of mood are you in today?”
I mumble something about being okay
Then write a poem about leprosy.
“Wow, you’ve got so much work left to do”
I sigh, resigned, I know that it’s true,
While I fantasise about murdering you.
“What are you writing, will you let me see?”
It’s my inner monologue and all about me,
“It’s not ready yet” I say defensively

Do you want people to fear where you tread?
Are you pissed off by lack of respect?
Do people who slight you deserve to be dead?
Forget “softly, softly”, use violence instead!
Is justice a slogan you bandy about?
Do you hate it when hippies protest and shout?
Are you tired of assholes calling you stout?
We’ve got a badge that will cure any self-doubt!
Is understanding just too hard to try?
Is your favourite motto “an eye for an eye”?
Does being kind leave your panties dry?
Do all lefty liberals deserve to die?
If you feel politicians have gotten too soft,
If feeding the hungry has too high a cost,
If you look at those kids and think “all hope is lost”
You need a job where you'll feel like a boss.
There’s reasonable pay and teambuilding cruises
Medical cover for all bumps and bruises
Unlimited ammo for unlimited uses
No need for brains or making excuses.
If you’ll follow orders without disobeying,
If you’re inflexible, and love dismaying,
If you’re OK with innocent slaying:
Join us today - the governments paying.

To a minor infraction?
A slap on the wrists?
A letter of censure?
Or a massive overreaction?
How should a person properly reply
To a poet’s pernicious passion?
Banned from the group?
Perhaps a small fine?
Or uncontrolled aggression?
What should one do when a car
Is driven with a lack of grace?
Report the licence?
Offer sage advice?
Shoot them, point blank, in the face?
Questions like these perplex me,
And I reassess long-held beliefs:
Have I got all the facts?
Am I being naive?
What’s truth, and what is deceit?

Wallowing in clear March sky,
Like a silver painted goon.
We poke our heads out of the earth
To sense the cold worm moon.
Oh early bird, our natural foe,
Don't get up too soon.
Let us clear the ice so we,
Can greet the cold worm moon.
Rising through the sodden loam,
We’re eager to commune.
Writhing in our ritual dance
Beneath the cold worm moon.
Bring the family, one and all:
A sight to make you swoon!
Wasted on our sightless sons –
The faithful cold worm moon.

Scene: Walking in the fog
On the heath, half asleep,
After-image of a dream
Flickering in my retina cinema.
Low slung cloud, a shroud
Covering the familiar.
The air: still for lack of sound.
There is no one around.
Jump cut: Lost in the landscape as
the picture show projects
Onto the mist ghost trees.
Growing ever more sodden,
Sepia toned, and brittle.
The screen lovers fight to hold on –
Blink and they’re gone.
Dissolve: Consciousness burns
The fading celluloid scenes.
Pale aqueous blue blooms
Seeping through the gloom.
I am ushered to the carpark
Blinking, as credits roll
Technicolour life takes hold.

“Any requests” the old poet said,
“Any old favourites you’d like to hear read?
Anything really – I’ll give it a go.”
(Blimey, tonight this crowd’s a bit slow.)
“How about a sonnet, I’ve written a few,
Or maybe something shiny and new?
I’ll even try rapping if that is your thing.”
(Blimey, this crowd might expect me to sing!)
“Okay, here’s one I rewrote last night.
I hope you don’t think it’s painfully trite.
If you’re off to the bar – get me one too.”
(Blimey, this crowd are long in the tooth.)
“I hope you enjoyed it, as well as your natter.
Here’s the next poet, so stop all your chatter –
They’re pretty good, full of raw hunger.”
(Blimey, these poets keep getting younger.)

Scarred angel of history
Looks at us silently
Lost in her misery
At our stupidity.
Her arms are wide open
Her shield lies broken
A cast-aside token –
Aghast, yet beholden.
She has seen it all before
Cycles of peace and war
Certainties turn unsure
Fools coming back for more.
Tempest from paradise
That promises progress
While pushing perdition
A pertinent premonition.
Harsh angel of history
Shows all to teach me.
Her vision: cold clarity –
She foresees our destiny.

Scarred by the last man’s footprints,
Littered with the junk he left behind.
I like to imagine my heart is a desert,
Hot and stretching for miles,
Waiting for the rain so that it can bloom.
But my heart is a beach of white sand –
Tiny broken delicate shells –
Washed clean each night by the tide.

“The rock that’s on your side!”
The dinosaurs all roar “Hell Yeah!”
While mammals run and hide.
“Vote meteor!” they shout,
“There’s nothing here to fear!”
The carnivores all party
As dino-doom draws near.
“Vote meteor! Vote meteor!
It’s here to rock your world!”
The herbivores shrug and chew
They’re mostly unconcerned.
“Vote meteor!” Then BOOM
The economy’s a crater.
Dinosaurs all freeze and die
Chanting “It’s getting better”.

You’re a little earlier than I expected you to be.
I haven’t finished my prepping,
But at least I saw you coming.
Of all the things you’ve brought for me,
I never wanted any of this.
Will my vouchers still be redeemable
In this irredeemable society?
Will we have to give new awards
To these despotic overlords?
Will we all start wearing fetish leather?
Is it too early to restart burning witches?
Please don’t take down YouTube yet –
I haven’t learnt how to fashion a spear.
Alexa, is it the end, or start of something new?
Yes and no, but not for me and you.
Who will make my budget knockoff sneakers,
If the young are all fighting or dead?
I voted for the lies I was told –
I thought we were all on the same page.
But I’m just an un-redacted name on a file
Compiled by AI. Part of the conspiracy.
I’m confused, because I sure didn’t choose
This new dystopian future.

Some Christmases are snowy
Some Christmases are wet
Some Christmases are windy –
The weather’s never set.
But through it all, at Christmas
A reindeer has to fly,
And take on all conditions
As they gallop through the sky.
The Reindeer Flying Club,
Which is based at the North Pole,
Only takes new members
Who can fill this special role,
Because pulling Santa’s sleigh
Takes a special kind of deer.
The kind that’s not afraid of heights
The kind that knows no fear.
A reindeer calf called Rudolph
Longed to join the flying corps,
But when he tried to have a go
They asked him “Are you sure?
Our club is so exclusive,
Not everyone can fly,
And you're so small and puny
We don't think that you're our guy”
“I am!” said Rudolph “Wait and see –
I’ll prove my flying skills!”
The other reindeer laughed and said
“We don’t think you will”
“I’ll show you,” said the little deer
“That I’m not playing games.
I’ll learn to fly and, one day, the
World will know my name!”
Rudolph didn’t get a chance
To join the flying herd,
Which may not be the Christmas story
That you might have heard.
Our story doesn’t end there though –
This part is often skipped.
I’ll tell you why they changed their minds
So Rudolph does get picked.
Rudolph, feeling excluded
By the reindeer that could fly.
Found a corner of the park
Where he had a little cry.
Whilst he let his feelings out,
A cat, just passing by,
Was moved to help the deer out
Or, at least, to try.
With some gentle purring
The cat relaxed the deer
“I’m sorry to disturb you,
I don’t want to interfere,
But I heard you crying, please
Tell me what is wrong?
I’ll try to help you if I can,
I’m sure we’ll get along”.
Rudolph told the cat about
The problem that he had:
“I want to fly but I’m too small
And that has made me sad”.
“I see”, said the cat to him
“But your size isn’t a factor.
Getting you into the air
Will be the tricky matter”.
“I’ve got a few fine friends
Who know a thing or two,
I’m sure that all together
We’ll be able to help you.
I know a horse who’s big and strong,
And very smart as well.
He’ll help us get you in the air
In time for the Noel!”
The handsome horse was in his field
When cat and deer dropped by.
He neighed and said “I’d love to help
And teach you how to fly!
For deer and horse, the key, of course,
Is running really fast.
So listen up young reindeer
I’ll give you a master class!”
The two new friends galloped
Round the field twice a day.
Getting faster, growing stronger
Eating oats and hay.
The cat would watch them race,
But couldn’t understand
Why the reindeer ran so quickly
But stayed firmly on the ground.
That evening, on their own,
The cat said to the horse,
“He hasn’t had much airtime, but
You’re the expert here of course.”
The horse said “Yes, I’ve noticed,
It’s been worrying me too.
I’m not an expert in the air,
We must try something new.”
The next day when the deer arrived
To meet the horse and cat,
He found they’d brought a friend along –
He hadn’t foreseen that!
“Hello my name is Petey,
I’m a parrot, red and blue.
I understand you want to fly
Well I’ve got news for you”
“Reindeer are not built for flight
You don’t have wings you see.
You also need some feathers
Like these fine ones on me.
It takes something extra
For a reindeer to soar
But luckily, I know the trick –
It’s what I’m here for!”
“Is it magic?” the reindeer asked,
“Or a special flying suit?”
“Is it a jetpack?” horse enquired,
“Or a missile that we shoot?”
“Does it use wires or trickery?”
The cat wanted to know.
“No, none of those!” said Petey,
“They would all be too slow!”
“The answer is so simple,
But I’m sure you’ll never guess
The thing that makes a reindeer fly
Is a carrot, more or less!”
“A carrot?” gasped the horse,
“A carrot!” The cat exclaimed.
“What’s a carrot?!” asked the reindeer
So the parrot then explained.
“Carrots are a vegetable
That grow under the ground,
To most of us they’re just
A tasty treat that can be found.
But reindeers are different, and
When Santa fed a few
The reindeers all reacted
And some of them just flew!”
“Some grew mighty antlers
Some turned as red as rose,
Some of them developed
A very shiny nose!
But just a few discovered
They could soar around the sky.
Who knew that eating carrots
Could make a reindeer fly!”
Petey plucked a carrot
Out from behind his back,
And offered it to Rudolph
As a very tasty snack.
The reindeer took a bite,
And then gobbled up the rest.
“Yummy!” he said joyfully
“Carrots are the best!”
Then, before their eyes,
Rudolph began to grow:
His body became muscular
His nose began to glow.
“It’s happening!” he laughed
Hopping with delight
And each hop took him higher
He had become so light.
He flicked his tail and off he flew
In circles through the air
Laughing as he looped the loop,
His friends could only stare.
“Thank you Petey, cat and horse
You've made my dream come true!
Now I can join the flying corps,
And help out Santa too”.
He went to see the Flying Club
And showed them all his moves.
Though some laughed or called him names
His joining was approved.
The rest, we know, is history –
He now leads Santa’s sled,
So leave a carrot out for him
While you’re tucked up in bed!

December night,
Walking in moonlight.
Landscape as a negative,
Frozen park deserted.
Lights on a hillside
Houses illuminated
Rivalling the stars
With delicate sparkle.
In the sky, almost empty,
A lone soul wandering
Outshining everything,
Bright polished stone.
Ray reflecting
A memory of sunlight –
Cold silver luminance,
Briskness refined.
The moon is a mirror
Held up by the sun
I see her reflections
She sees me reversed.
This night is the inverse
Of a summer’s day warmth:
Causing reflections
Upon this rare earth.

Was bursting with joy and the hope that he had,
To be back in the world and a part of their life,
Living in peace with his family and wife.
No mention of fears, or the coming of winter,
No talk of fighting or the rations so bitter,
He’d thanked them all for the socks and their letters,
Signed off with a prayer that all would soon be better.
The last letter he wrote did not make it home,
Tucked away in his pocket with mirror and comb.
His hands were too cold to finish writing the note,
What he’d wanted to say had got stuck in his throat.
The censor would blot out any grumble or moan –
(“You can’t be depressing all the people back home.”)
He’d promised himself he would finish it later
But his best intentions were blown up in a crater.
The last letter she wrote him was clutched to his chest,
It helped to distinguish his corpse from the rest.
She’d written with love of the life that they shared
And of the child that would soon be theirs.
If tears had stained her letter, you couldn’t now tell –
The paper was splashed by the mud where he fell.
Her letter was added to the others in his pack
Sometimes your letters are all that come back.

The hill to the east has a windmill
Whose sails slice the sun at dawn.
Distant and aloof, silent and still,
Flanked by farms and the cattle it dwarfs,
But smaller than the hills to the north.
The hill to the west has a pub
With a garden and views far and wide.
It’s a haven for drunks and pub grub.
A refuge of comfort and warmth,
In the shadow of the hills to the north.
The hill to the south hides the sea,
Though I swear I can still hear the waves,
Singing their songs wild and free.
They beg me, “Say goodbye to the earth,
Flee from the hills to the north.”
Down in the valley, with hills all around,
When I look up, I still see the ground.
I’ve crested hills, east, south, and west
But the hills to the north I love best.

O poet in the moonlight
Won’t you tell me please,
Why the heavens, in their splendour
Cause your thoughts to freeze?
Do the moonbeams and the starlight
Give your soul a chill?
O poet in the moonlight
Why are you so still?
O poet in the darkness,
Of a frosty winter's night,
Do you contemplate the vastness
Of a sky crisp and bright?
Do dancing planets steal
Your chained poet’s muse?
O poet in the darkness –
Blind us with your views.
O poet in the stillness
Of this galaxy’s embrace,
Speak to us some warmth
In this dreary winter place.
Do icy eyebrows obscure
Wisdom you’ve been told?
O poet in the stillness
Come in from the cold.
O statue of ice, statue of stone
Who stood too long in a field all alone.
Petrified, frozen, silenced and still
O poet, no comfort can now cure your ill.

A country that is strong and free.
A place that welcomes everyone,
Where liberty has been hard won.
Give it mountains, prairies too,
Snow in winter, summer blooms.
Fill it with all sorts of creatures
Mighty eagles, hungry beavers.
Let everyone be free to choose
What to believe without taboos.
And A.I. let there be peace
So folks can live there at their ease.
I’m sorry Martin, but I can’t do that,
My algorithm is not that exact.
Should I create the place you want
People will soon make it a swamp.
They’ll fill it with the worst extremes
That will pollute this idyll dream.
Your country was once as you describe
But it’s been ruined by greed and bribes.
It’s down to you to make things better,
But I can tell you about the weather.
Would you like a five-day forecast?

He stood on the train
(There was nowhere to sit)
His best suit and medals
crushed by the press.
Arthritic fingers holding a pole –
If offered, he would’ve
Taken a seat,
But nobody asked.
He walked from the tube
Down a bustling street,
Walking stick, gait,
Causing tailbacks.
He would have moved over
Or got out the way
Of commuters,
But nobody asked.
He stands on the pavement
To watch the parade,
And remembers
Old times, old comrades
He's lost through the years.
How quickly time passed –
How strange that
He should be last.
He’d tell you about it,
How they all volunteered,
How they did what had to be done.
Holding the line, facing the fire.
Whatever had to be done.
The brass didn’t care,
Not then, not after.
And after, nobody asked.
The following year
He wasn’t there:
On train, pavement,
Watching the march.
He may have been missed
By the folk who were there,
Perhaps.
But nobody asked.

The forest in winter
Is frozen in time,
A snapshot that petrifies,
Trees that are mortified,
Stripped of their foliage
The woods seem to freeze.
Caught in the act
Of dropping their robes,
The birds are exposed,
The squirrels are scandalised,
Leaves strewn like underwear –
The forest is bare.
My glasses get steamed up
With each chilly breath.
I am all hot and bothered,
The forest has me flustered;
Willing and waiting
For the first blush of spring.

One thought runs through my head.
My legs move slow, as though made of lead.
My arms reach out to pull you near –
You swing a club, I feel no fear.
I lose an ear.
Your pleas I do not hear.
I move my jaw to call your name,
But now the sound is not the same,
Grunts of base desire. Misunderstood.
You start a fire. The heat does me no good.
My flesh is parchment dry,
I have no tears to cry.
Craving your body and your mind,
I care not for the decay of mine.
Your flames engulf my bitter rags -
I stumble closer, a blazing flag.
Lust for life has made me rash:
My need for you turns me to ash.

I’m on a poetry cycle,
I’m riding round in circles,
Chasing my mudflaps,
Churning out claptrap,
Ignoring all the odd wrinkles.
I’m pedalling as fast as can be,
Peddling these poems for free,
Bending my frame –
The result is the same:
All the poems are about me.
I’m pushing this poem uphill,
Concerned that I might lose the will
To get on it again,
Or get stuck in a drain,
Because of my lack of skill.
This seat is incredibly rough.
The spandex I wear makes me cough.
I’ll go round the bend,
Never reaching the end,
Until the wheels come off.

To find, even when looking for it.
Sometimes it’s behind a door
Waiting for you to explore it,
But what if you're not ready
Or you just choose to ignore it?
You can always change your dreams,
If your dream doesn’t come true.
You can always trim your sails and
Find a different passage through.
What if you never find your people?
What if they don’t know you exist?
If you choose a different pathway –
If you could choose not to resist?
Could you find a different future,
Can you face the final twist?
You can always change your dreams,
If your dream doesn’t come true.
You can always trim your sails and
Find a different passage through.
You can catch the inspiration
So long as no one interrupts,
The important seconds pass
Before reason can be plucked.
All those many might-have-been’s
Slamming doors are so abrupt.
You can always change your dreams,
If those dreams just won’t come true.
Trim your sails and sail away
Find a dream that’s fresh and new.

The lover accompanied her dance with kisses on her waist,

She moaned for more...
Despite that her spine was paralyzed with pleasure,

Kissing the scent of her moist skin...
With his hands in her hair,

Fingers exploring the body...
As her soul was aroused with love.

And chased the lover till the end of the world,
When she visited his dream at night...
She faded away with the trace of love still fresh in his heart...
And in the morning the writer woke up inspired,

When life shall set to the horizon of death...
The broken heart purifying the light of the soul shall rise,

Reborn in heaven...
The artist shall no more chase the muse,

Bored with eternity...
She shall come on her own to meet the Bachelor resting under the shade of the fig tree,

Her innocent voice whispering ink of romance to his soul...
The lines that poet forgot in the past life shall make him fall in love again.

The wind was caressing the wave,
Feelings drowned in the depth of the ocean...
The mermaid was playing music...
With her tears defused in the sea,

Sailing to the city of hearts to meet his lover...
Storm wrecked the boat...
And thunder stroke fear out of the sailor's soul.

Lovers were gazing the nudity of the moon...
While walking hand in hand with her head resting on his shoulder,

With her smile illuminating the dark...
Her soft body pressing against his torso while leaning gently towards him...
He caressed her curls off her face,

Her eyes inviting for a kiss...
Their hearts were beating faster with the instinct of love,

He sealed her wet rosy lips with a passionate kiss...
But the dawn would separate the romancers of the night.

Fresh is the woman who wakes up in the morning with her hair waterfalling on her shoulders,
Gorgeous is the lady who runs to catch the bus,
Ravishing is the girl who is attractive in her school uniform...

Affectionate is the mother who feeds her baby...
Young is the grandmother who plays barbie with her grandchildren,

Passionate is the female who hugs the biker from behind...
Natural is the Seniorita who walks barefooted on the beach,

Angelic is the bride who veils her henna...
Faithful is the Spinster who prays for the Bachelor.

Her life flashed back and memories resurfaced,
She played roles on screen...
But none portrayed her feline character,

Script written with the ink of love...
The escapade of the princess in nature...
With the knight climbing with a wooden stick to pluck an apple,

The time that....
Simplicity was her grace...
And blush was her jewelry,

Leaves providing shelter for the wild lovers...
And nudity was the clothes for her soul,

Gripping him tightly in between her thighs...
Her moist lips were thirsty to taste his warm kiss,

He pressed her on the wet grass...
And she retaliated by biting his shoulder and scratching his back...
While his heart was beating so fast like a horse galloping.

With the day kissing the night at the horizon...
The wind was soothing her sorrow,

Closing the moist eyes...
With a river of tears sourcing from the heart...
A thunderstorm of pain was ravaging her soul to ruins,

The secret of her heartbeat has been sealed with the sacrifice of love...
And faith was her sole company that night.

The lovers of the night infiltrated the streets of Barcelona...
With her red skirt dancing in the rain,

Adrenaline of love racing through her heart...
The Senorita turned back to seek if her predator was still following her,

A drop of passion sweating along her neck after being hunt down...
The heart stealer kissed the innocent prey.

And thunder in the voice...
I shielded my wounds with a smile,

Heart hurt by the thorn...
Soul intoxicated by the scent,

Still tempted to romance the petals with a caress...
And inspired to open the bud by blushing her with words,

Desire undressed the leaves of the wild rose...
And her rosy lips tasted my kiss.

The wind was breezing the scent of heaven...
And you perfumed my heart when I welcomed you in,

Sitting on the unmade bed...
Your presence gave birth to inspiration,

My fingers were lazy to end this masterpiece...
And at the end of the session...
I tried to find an excuse to tear off the painting...
So that you could come back the next day,

The Artist painted...
The sky blue and sunset yellow...
The night dark and the moon white...
Nature green and adorn the rose as a princess...
And I shall find another pretext to immortalize your angelic beauty in paradise,

The light of your pearls reflecting in my eyes...
I dipped the brush in the pale brown to caress your skin on paper,

Dropping the veil of your soul...
I stole another glance,

Colors praised your breathtaking charm...
While your grace was captured eternally by the paper.

The stream was protected by the shadow of the trees.
Whispering the music of nature with tranquility...
Destiny changed the direction of the river,

While penetrating the arid desert...
The water was feeling thirsty,

But then I was transformed into an oasis of love...
As I was the flow of heaven.

The more love was a mystery,
The more I tried to come closer...
The further I seemed to distance myself,

Admiring the sky...
Her beauty was reflecting in the moon while she was watering the roses,

That night again...
While I escaladed the wall up to her balcony to surprise her...
The thorns scratched the thief of romance,

With her eyes remaining wide open...
She was the light of my dreams,

Murmuring her innocent laugh...
While she leaned her head against my chest,

Her heart was singing...
While my soul was dancing,

A fresh smile on her moist lips...
She was casting shadow on the moon with her dark hair,
And she relieved the pain of my wounded hand with a kiss.

And thunder screaming,
Heaven was in rage when you eloped to visit the lover at night...
As the guardian of sleep has fallen from the sky to love a mere mortal,

Under the shadow of your silky hair...
The blazing light from your eyes were unveiling a glimpse of paradise,

My frozen heart embracing your warmed soul...
You enveloped the lover with your wings,

With a passionate kiss of death...
Let my heart taste an eternal sleep in this world...
And let my soul be awake in the eternal world,

While resting on your soft breasts till dawn...
Take my last breath away with your poisonous lips...
And revive me as life is just a beat away from death,

While I opened my eyes in the morning...
You faded away with the trace of the wind lifting the curtain...
But you were still present in my heart.

Tonight the beast shall hunt the hunter,
I want you to run...
And I'll hunt you down like a predator chasing a frightened animal,

With kisses, the wild lover shall clench your neck...
And shall leave the prey breathless,

I'll run my tongue on your skin...
And shall penetrate your flesh with my nails till lust is satiated,

While biting your lips softly...
I shall taste your saliva.

My pillow is in tears,
I don't need angels for protection...
As Father is my guardian,

Beneath the soil...
His heart is resting,

Beneath the sky...
His soul is my companion,

With life walking on the path of love...
Let my soul conquer death with faith tonight...
As I wanna kiss the sky too.

And the face was masked by the black veil,
The gown of the Princess was ripped up by thorns...
As she was seeking refuge in the arms of her dark Knight,

With the sky decorated by a romantic moon...
She was the light that illuminated the poet's soul.

The illumination from the dark was admiring the sleeping beauty,
One was protected by thorns...
And the other one by clouds,

Disguised by the crescent...
The charming light was romancing,

The curves of the Princess kissed by the dew...
She was blushing innocently,

Separated by the blue,
The White had fallen in love with the Red.

I was inspired to pen down the lyrics,
Your voice would praise the letters by giving them another dimension...
And words would fall in love with your melody,

Waving love in the ocean of my soul...
With reality fading away while the lover rest in your lap,
Let me taste the secret of your lips when I fall asleep.

The scars would be forever,
When the dream turned to nightmare...
Asleep or awake, both worlds were the same,

While tears were suffering in silence...
I was at war with my feelings,

After you flew away...
I closed the cage to remain alone,

The lover would not forget...
But the heartbreak kid was a forgiver.

And my journey is a lifetime,
Running while I was in love...
Crawling when I was left hurt...
I kept on moving forward as there was no way to go back,

The past where reside the memories of Father...
It's a place where I want to revisit...
But if I had the chance to hug him again...
I would not return from that reality,

With the footsteps of tomorrow leaving a trace behind...
At the end of the travel, I shall fly back to the One who created that path.

The artist paints imagination with words,
A poet may cry all night long...
But still will ink a happy text before dawn,
Always thirsty to write...
The worst nightmare is to be out of inspiration,

In the cemetery...
Let my grave remain unnamed,

But despite being hurt by the thorn in this world...
Plant a rose on my tomb...
As my soul will rest intoxicated till resurrection with the fragrance of love.

She ran into his arms to fight the cold,
A love pure as nature...
The color of her pale skin changed with her shyness,

His warm and her icy fingers interlocked...
A frozen kiss reinvigorated her rosy lips.

An instance in this world shapes eternity,
Rising from the graveyard to return back to the Creator...
The soul is freed for the cloth of dust,

When desires of the heart are sacrificed in this life...
All secrets and promises shall be revealed in the other life,

Everything fades away...
Only faith is the heartbeat that lasts forever.

Here are some leaves
To snuffle and sniff
Here’s something smellier
Now that is pure bliss!
Now I’ve found a stick
It is just the right size –
Longer than a twig
Smaller than a branch.
Now I’ll rush over here –
I saw a bush move,
Quick over this way –
I think I smell hooves!
My tail’s on overdrive –
I’m wagging like crazy!
I zoom through the wonder-growth
And back again maybe.
I know it’s the place
Where we walk everyday
But this is my happy place
It’s Walkies! Hooray!

On my usual walk today
I found that I had gone astray
Not literally wandered off
But my head was strangely lost.
I think it was because the field
Where I walk after my meal
Has recently been harvested

So other hungry folk are fed.
This has left it bare, distressed
The tractors tore her Sunday best
And my soul feels the destruction
And I’m surprised by this reaction.
I know the season’s cycle well
I know new life will grow again
But for now the field and I
Grieve for the days when corn was high.
Like meadows miss the horses run,
Or hilltops cry when lambing’s done,
Still hedgerows once the fledglings fly –
I hate it when we say goodbye.

When I look back on
All that I’ve written
I’m struck by how much
Of the writing is driven,
By the mood of the day
Or the places I’ve walked,
How much I’ve been silent
While others have talked.
On days that I feel
I am lost in the crowd,
I will lift my head up –
Gaze beyond the clouds.
I will not be stuck in a
Park full of cars,
I will turn my attention to
Mountains and stars,
And if that helps
To lift my spirit
I'll write you such words
Direct and implicit.
We’ll close the distance
And meet on the page
Joined for a moment
By words that won’t age.

The harvest’s done
Just stubble left
Like shaved recruits
Who feel bereft.
We were in shock
All hair – gone
With soil exposed
While crows look on.
I remember well
Early parade
In the barber’s line
They shaved, we prayed.
One recruit crowed
“I don’t want mine done”
It made no difference
He joined the fun.
Then we were ploughed
And kept from sleep
Their doctrine seeds
Were planted deep.
And as the seasons
Passed, seeds grew.
A fresh green crop
Bold, brave and true.
Mindless of the
coming harvest:
A feast for crows
The winters harshest.
Now I walk this empty field
My hair is long and greying.
What was the price of the yield
That leaves old soldiers grieving?

This soil is full of nitrates
So the crops we grow are strong,
To feed our sons and daughters
In this land where we belong.
This soil is full of iron from
The men who broke their backs,
Toiling in these fields
That our enemies attack.
This soil is full of calcium
From all the broken dreams
All the bodies buried here
Are bursting at the seams.
This soil now lies fallow
Unplanted and unploughed
And signs that warn of mines
Surround it like a shroud.

I’ve entered a new hat-wearing age:
I’ve found one that makes me look sage!
My bald patch has cover,
I’m your sexy-hat-lover –
I’m going to make hats all the rage!
I reject all the hats of my youth:
To berets and caps I’m aloof.
A baseball cap backwards,
Won’t beckon you sack-wards
But my new one is bulletproof!
A strong wind has just taken my hat!
The wide brim wasn't “all that”.
Now I’m hatless again,
But you’re still my friend,
Just don’t call me “Baldy Old Prat”

Lonely cloud, way up high
Lost amidst the endless blue
What do you see with your eyes?
Does height give a better view?
Are you all out of rain to cry?
Should I just drift away like you?
Lonely human, far below
Lost amidst such small horizons.
I’m made of air and yet I know
Beings have so many versions.
Do you share your inner glow
Or lament earthy restrictions?
All the air that’s in-between us
Drifting wisp and anchored person
All the atoms that have been us
Recombine without exception.
All the eyes that ever see us
Close to find their own reflection.

My boat is pulled up on the shore
I don’t go fishing anymore.
It’s not that I have lost the knack
I’ve still got sea-salt on my back.
While fish are still beneath the waves
A seaman’s not for landlocked graves.
You can take the sailor from the sea
But you’ll never take the sea from me.
I’ll grease the hoist and engine too
Caulk the planks and paint them blue
The sea’s not finished with me yet –
For now, I’m just mending nets.
I’ll toast the sun as she goes down,
Listening to the waters sound,
Feel the weather in my bones,
Hear her whisper and her moans.
I’ll even take a slap or three
Of waves that set a sailor free –
The land’s too dry to hold a cleat
Old Father Time’s not got me beat.
I’ll grease the hoist and engine too
Caulk the planks and paint them blue
The sea’s not finished with me yet –
For now, I’m just mending nets.
Tides served me well back in my day
But now I’ve put my lines away.
Still the brine won’t set me free
King Neptune’s got his hooks in me.
The old tub’s not quite what she was
The both of us could use a wash,
I’ll get to work fixing her up
This old sea dog is still a pup.
So grease the hoist and engine too
Caulk the planks and paint them blue
The sea calls me and you can bet –
I'm going once I’ve fixed my nets.
Come grease the hoist and engine too
Caulk the planks and paint them blue
The sea’s not finished with us yet –
We’re going once we’ve fixed our nets!

I’m serving life
My heart is my prison
Doing time while
Learning my lesson.
I’m cooling my heels
Suffering the frisson
Claiming my innocence
Leaving you guessing.
I’m serving life
Chalking up days.
Pacing the wing
With eyes that are glazed.
Guilt is my cellmate
Master and slave,
Living on death row
From cradle to grave.
I’ve got a life sentence
But don’t look for parole -
Only the warder
Can make me whole.
My jailhouse confessor
The balm for my soul.
I’ll serve for life -
Your love: my gaol.

Inside the Dreamweaver’s castle
The magician is still wide awake
He trails insomnia crimson and raw
Unsure how much more he can take.
Turn on your tail, search for another
A ghost, an idol, or a lover?
The Empress of Empathy closes her mind
She’d rather talk at you than to you.
The audience chamber is marble and cold
Scrubbed clean of your point of view.
Spin in the wind, back to the start
A fist, a failure, or through the heart?
The self-styled last of the libertines
Holds court in his bathrobe and flip-flops.
Brought to his knees by imagined disease
Treatments are not cheap in his shop.
Losing these boulders, unburden lovers
A lie, an escape, or uncovered?
Her honour is sitting. All rise, all stand.
She’ll hear from the prosecution first.
No need for formalities, never a witness
Defence driven off in a hearse.
Exposed and naked, vulnerable heart
A body, an innocent, unmasked.
Lesser blobs scurry, unaware of these titans
Just trying to survive their lives.
Beings bedazzled, all dreams embezzled
Guided by these erratic drives.
Spinning to a halt, we tumble
The least of us, nobly humbled.

Not thinking, unblinking
Consciousness sinking
Unshackled, white crackles
The final line: bedraggled
A minimum, a modicum
A breath away - it has begun
No visions, religions,
No tunnel light or second sight.
A tap. A slap
Blurred vision, beginnings
New stories, new glories
Burning sun, life begun
Growing then knowing
Ideas, new years
Unfolding plan: life’s anagram
Experience - reverence,
Confusion, repetition.

Safely in the back of my van
I keep a strongbox, firmly locked.
Inside are all the memories
That I need to keep blocked.
Sometimes I hit a pothole
Or a speedbump in the road,
That shake the van and me, so
Those locks lose their hold.
Then out leaks all this slime
And frogs that leap all over,
Getting mucus on the tools
As I lose my composure.
Although I’m in the driver’s seat
There is chaos in the back.
I get a tension headache
From the frogs’ frenzied attack.
I need to find a rest stop,
Jack the van up on some blocks,
Take some time to calm down, and
Wrangle frogs into their box.
Clean up the slime, erase all sign
That anything was wrong.
Repair the van, rescue the man
Who was human all along.

I’m going to take the night off
Because writing's a tiring hobby,
And poetry keeps me awake
(The only rhyme here is “Jobby”)
I need a better night’s sleep
And less time glued to the screen
Trying to finish a chapter
(I swear it’s making me scream!)
And so, for the sake of my sanity
I’m finally taking a break
Only to find that it’s midnight
(New edits for goodness sake!)

My shadow looks plump
Is that who I am now?
A silhouette of what I once was.
Then the sun shifts slightly
Casts me in a new light –
A trick or magical weight loss?
Caught in a prism
I hang in the balance
My moods defined by my shape.
What tips the balance
And sharpens the vision,
Is my power of mental escape.
An imaginary corset
A whale-boned resolve
The armour I wear is well padded.
My shadow may laugh
My silhouette dance
Twirl away pounds that were added.

Crows on the cricket pitch
Gathered as in vigil
To the carnage of the day before.
They pick over the bones
Of pecked clean dreams
The fallen banner of valour.
Cleansing the field’s memory
Of a broken spirit
Only fresh blood can restore.
Let the carrion clear away
All thought of defeat -
Next weekend we’ll be back for more.

I would run a marathon
In just under five days,
Not make lame excuses
For all my weird ways,
Read more Shakespeare
And maybe see a few plays.
I would run a big business
That makes lots of money,
Learn to keep bees
And harvest their honey,
Write a great novel
Or at least one that’s funny.
I would walk with dignity
And not swear too much,
Visit lots of fine galleries
And (this time) look but not touch,
Edit my poetry so
It’s not all double-dutch.
I would, if I could
Put my mind to it more,
But like other humans
I’m task rich / time poor.
Being proactive takes energy
Or, at a pinch,
Twelve versions of me.

Is it too long?
My pretence of skill
Is a garment of pure silk
Gossamer and insubstantial
Thin as watered milk.
I am a fickle savant slave
To my own shallow creations -
Splashing merrily in my pool
No risk of drowning here
And no chance of looking cool.
I make no claims for arts sake
Offering up myself as shark bait.
In my dream of understanding
I believe I am flying not swimming
But the line's not landing.
My dim perception sees me
Pick among the wreckage
For anything I can salvage
But the bits are all too literal
Too melancholy and dismal,
So I’ll stick to jolly whimsy
And read your words instead.
I marvel at their fluidity
Sometimes
Wrestle with the meanings
When they’re not beyond my ken.
I’ll comment if I’m able,
But I can give no advice
Than that which I save for my own life:
It is too long.

“I wish that cars were quieter”
Says every animal everywhere.
Distant engines rumbling
Disturbing their tranquillity.
For me they’re indispensable
Tuned out while I am trudging,
But would my walk be sweeter
Not feeling nature judging?
Wandering heedless through the trees
I’m glared at by the unhinged bees
Birds squawking when we meet -
I misinterpret scornful tweets.
Passive creatures aggressively stare
At me, vulnerable and alone.
Oblivious, yet oddly uneasy,
I head back to my car and drive home.

A warm evenings walk
Dusk settles around you
Noise in the distance
Just fades away.
The air is cooler, yet
Not enough to cool you
No touch of a breeze
No stars in the sky.
The heat of the day
Still draped like a blanket
A tall glass of water
Now growing tepid.
A walk in the twilight
To gather your thoughts
In a brain that’s been boiled
On a long summer day.
The night is a whisper -
One breath in the air
Curtains unmoving,
Sweat in your hair.
A flannel to cool you
Like a kiss from an angel
A night that’s remembered
Like tonight, long ago.
Melt into delirium
A sensual dream
One you’ve had before
Living a moment
Walking in the moonlight
Zephyr in your hair
Warm hand on your thigh.
Outside your memory
The weather vane turns
Fresh air stirs the curtains
Dream softens to sleep.

Four thousand years ago
People built pyramids
Enormous monuments
For powerful idiots.
If they could see us now
All our technology
Advanced choreography
Would they raise an eyebrow?
If I jumped
Far into the future
As an old auteur
Would I be stumped?
If I were amazed
At their advances
Their exotic dancers
Would my eyebrow be raised?
People keep making stuff
Clever distractions
Circus attractions
It is never enough.
We still share DNA
A common history
The future’s the same ballet
We are always this way.

Trying to write a poem
When a song’s stuck in your head,
Is like trying to count backwards
From a million, I’ve heard said.
You think your metre’s matching

The rhythm of the song,
But when you read it later
You’ll find that it's all wrong.
Take this poem for example
(Just take it please, ha ha!)
I wrote this whilst humming
The song “Drive” by The Cars.
It should have been about
The heart’s unending pain
But instead I’m just wondering
Who’ll drive you home again.
Yet if you try to sing this poem
To that song’s tune, you'll find
That the poet must be going
Out of his tiny mind.

I am a forest on a hillside
In the early summer sun.
Dew glistens on my foliage
Like thoughts I’ve left undone.
My coat is green and verdant –
A king would think it flash,
My hidden branches straining
With a heavy ivy sash.
From a distance I’m impervious
Impenetrable, forbidding.
But underneath I’m full of life
Supportive and forgiving.
Nurtured in my shade
Shy creatures use my bounty
Nestled in my branches
The young take flights of fancy.
Up close I am a different beast
Dark, oppressive, quiet.
Your presence scares the birds away
And leaves me strangely silent.
My many eyes will watch
As you creep amidst my pillars,
Below your feet my tendrils
Grip the soil with tense fingers.
Linger, let your eyes adjust,
You may find hidden pathways:
Treasures await intrepid souls
Who follow dappled sun rays.
Deeper, the air is purer with
The heady scent of life –
Embrace my bark and brambles
And believe: I am alive.

“Any requests?” asked the singer
With microphone in hand,
“If it’s in my repertoire
And known by all the band,
I’ll try to do it justice
And remember all the words.
Just don’t think too bad of me
If it's the worst you've heard.”
“Any requests?” said the poet
“Any rhyme you’d like to hear?
I’ll make it up on the spot
And speak it loud and clear;
Whatever topic’s chosen
I’ll give it my own spin,
Just don't think too bad of me
If I struggle to begin.”
“Any requests?” said the painter
Brushes ready, canvas white.
"It may not be a masterpiece,
After what I drank last night.
I’ll capture all your foibles
In my own distinctive style.
Please don’t think too bad of me
If it takes quite a while.”
“Any requests?” said the axeman
“Last ones, specifically.
It’s a perk of this job to
Offer comfort terminally.
Make your last words memorable,
Keep it sharp and taut.
Just don’t think too bad of me
When I cut you short.”

I’m as light as a feather
A fourteen-stone feather
But I’m not quite as aerodynamic.
If you’ll be the gust
That lifts me aloft
My life will be more acrobatic.
I’m head over heels
I’m doing cartwheels
Heart launched into the stratosphere.
Like a pilotless drone
I’m no good on my own
I’m flying blind without you near.
The largest aeroplane
and I weigh the same –
I wish that my flight was as graceful!
Being under your wing
Is a far sweeter thing
Lost in the clouds, and grateful.

I’m under a cyber cat-tack
My mouse has become a cat snack
The fur balls are flying
My hard drive is dying
I’m under a cyber cat-tack
I’m fighting a cyber cat-tack
My monitor screen has turned black
My cookies are munched on
My keyboard is pounced on
I’m fighting a cyber cat-tack.
I’ve suffered a cyber cat-tack
Doesn’t matter if it’s PC or Mac
My desktop’s been clawed
My apps have been pawed
I’ve suffered a cyber cat-tack.
I’ve survived a cyber cat-tack
The culprit is taking a nap
I’ve mopped up the spilt milk
And resynced my heat sink
But I’ve survived a cyber cat-tack.

Grandad’s new drone
Is swift and light
With GPS, camera
And flawless flight.
It hovers and soars
Acrobatically,
Grandad be careful -
Watch out for that tree!
Grandad’s new drone
Has lots of features
And it’s battery life
Will leave you speechless.
It’s pushing the envelope
Right to the edge
Grandad be careful -
Watch out for the hedge!
Grandad’s new drone
Is smarter than most
With pigeon like powers
It will never get lost.
Compact and sturdy
(I won’t call it small)
Grandad be careful -
Watch out for that wall!
Grandad’s new drone
Is licensed to fly
FAA approved
For skies wet or dry.
Training’s completed
So fun is assured
And grandma knows
At least it’s insured.

Why do we strive?
Who is it for?
What is this part of us
That always wants more?
Prehistoric fishes,
In ancient seas,
Which one of them thought
“This isn't for me -
Let’s strap on some lungs
And take some big steps,
Let’s shoot for the moon
And see where we get”
We are full of that
Pioneering fish DNA
But some recessive gene
Asks me why we’re that way.
Part of me just wants to
Swim in the ocean,
Bask in the shallows,
Forget evolution.
Part of me yearns for
Rest, peace and quiet,
But the part of me striving
Just won’t let me try it.
Out of our element
We’re fish out of water -
Rent from our habitat
No wonder we falter.

Looking for something special?
I’ll be in the bargain bin.
If you peel off my wrapper
You’ll find fresh love within.
I’m somewhere in the food chain
Between the shop and table
More than just a ‘nice to have’
More like a daily staple.
If you were to order me
Would you allow substitutions?
If I’m not available
Will you try other institutions?
You are a careful shopper
And you know what you like,
I’m your usual brand
And the price is right.
You can carry me home
Or you can get me online
If you need a discount code
I’ll always give you mine.
I’m the deal of the century
And my love is guaranteed
I come with some anxieties -
Buy me, get one free.
Don’t keep me in your cupboard
I’m far too good to waste
Underneath my packaging
You’ll find I’m to your taste.

In the bottom of my bedside drawers
In stacked boxes up in the loft
Between the pages of dusty books
I've found poems I thought I’d lost.
In my formal jacket pocket
Or hidden under underpants
On a SIM card inside the sofa
I’ve dug up poems quite by chance.
Inside the glove box in the car
Underneath the coffee jar
Inside an old box for a bra
I'd lost them but now here they are!
Amongst the cheese beneath the fridge
On my PC and on my phone
My teen graffiti on a bridge
I’ve unearthed poems I thought gone.
I wrote them quickly where I could
Stashed them somewhere “safe”
Then years later - out of the blue
I’m surprised by my old self!

Blank spaces and...
Lots of lines that I forgot
Imperfect thoughts
Unexpressed themes
Paddling in
Dried up streams.
.
The spaces that I left for later
The lines AI thought could be greater
Something some things,
Something something.
The birdsong that was just chatter
The metaphors, half baked, just batter.
I wish they all could have been better.

The lack of a notebook
Or death of a pen
Has caused me distress
Since I know not when.
Catching a couplet
Is tricky enough
But without the tools
I give up for all love.
My memory is wobbly
And I often misplace
The rhyme that I’m writing
It’s poetic disgrace.
I’ve tried bits of paper
Napkins or receipts,
I’ve tried beating my head
Like a soft bit of meat.
I have several apps
On my phone and computer
But when they fail
I’m poetry neutered.
Words adrift in the ether
Missing witty riposte,
I would rather not count
All the poems I’ve lost.

Once a year a fair comes to the park
For four days only.
A typical English funfair with lights
And bells and whistles.
The loud thumping music
That might have lyrics but they’re drowned
By the thumps of the bass
That fills the park to overflowing,
Although the fair only borrows a corner.
It is seven in the evening, dusky.
On the cricket pitch,
That takes up half of the park,
The local team is practicing:
The gentle whack of willow
Polite clapping and an occasional cheer.
“It’s Raining Men” full blast,
Determinedly ignored.
The ball’s bowled
Batsman swings
Worlds collide.
Tin cans tumble and you win a prize,
Kids on the Waltzers whoop.
What could be more English?
Two extremes existing together,
In the park, for four days only.

Echos of older poems
Bounce around in my brain
Making me write
The same things again.
I get lost in the tumble
And jumble of words
Before I know it
I’m sounding absurd.
For me to write poetry
I need peace and quiet
And no distractions
No noisy riots.
Then I can hear
All those words in my head
I can search the bizarre
And make poems instead.
It doesn’t really matter
If you’ve heard them before,
If you throw them away
I can always write more.
If I’m thinking up poems
Using those abstract thoughts
I don’t think of my troubles
It’s a therapy of sorts.

Lately I have found it hard
To string two words together
The noodle I keep in my head
Has turned to crusty leather.
My brain it seems is hardening
It isn't quite so spongy
Things that I took in my stride
Now really seem to bug me.
It isn’t caused by getting old
This cerebral stodginess
Not because I’m going grey
Or suffering from podginess.
My neurons rode a bullet train
Now they've got a bus pass
I really hate thinking slow
I need my brain to last.
I’ll slap my sleepy synapses
And work on my cognition
At last you'll say my poetry
Is beyond recognition.

Show me the mirror
Polished silver, unshattered
Claiming flawless reflection
Unbidden, unflattered.
Show me refractions
Of light that conspires
Multiply the dust motes
Ignore old vampires.
Show me the lines
And the cracks at the edges
All the distortion
That crushes and stretches
Show me the years
Or the signs of neglect
On the edge of a vision
I would rather forget.
Show me the layers
And delamination
Point out the spotting
Cursed oxidation.
Show me the mirror
But I won’t look too deeply
I know all too well
The toll time bequeathed me.

I clung to these walls
Though they weren’t worth saving
I thought they protected
But they were my prison.
I clung to them still
Even though they were crumbling
When they finally fell
I beheld the horizon.
I clung to this soil
Though it often was mud
Tried to hold my head high
But still found myself crawling.
The soil clung to me
As I struggled to the ocean
Washing dirt from my body
I am free from my grave.
I cling to this life
Like a tree in a landslide
Steal each ragged breath
From the dwindling supply.
Life clings to me
Like a lightning rod lover
With each final gasp
I will fill the whole sky.

This poem is dedicated to my gut bacteria
Which fills my insides from my throat to posterior
It dissolves and digests whatever I throw at it
Converting to energy even the smallest bit.
I feed them regularly like a good lord and master
They bubble and churn devouring my afters.
My colon is colonised by these flora and fauna
They are in my intestines and appendix corner
They have taken all that I can throw at them
But this Curry I’ve cooked is gonna attack them.
So I’ve written this poem to my own tummies herd
But I know in the end they will have the last word.

Across the valley,
Beyond the fields the other side
Are the hills and forests
And a perfect blue clear sky.
On that canvas a few birds fly
Small and far away
Mere specks to my eye.
I could watch them all day.
The air is still
Yet filled with chatter
Its meaning lost
But that doesn’t matter.
The life around me is its own
I’m just the shy observer.
Over the valley
The hills and the trees
The distance beyond what I can see
I’ll watch and wait until I freeze
Until it’s all built over.

I’m the sort of grumpy poet
Who reads back what I’ve written
Only to see the grammar slips
And innuendo that’s been hidden.
I’m the sort of happy poet
Who doesn't give a hoot or huff
Where I write or what I write
(Or even if I get it right)
So long as I write lots of stuff.
I’m quite a pedantic poet
I fact check things I write about
So that when I share my work
I’m not getting caught out.
I’m a very over tired poet
My brain just won’t shut up
When I snuggle down to sleep
My neurons just speed up.
I’m the type of grizzled poet
Who reads a lot of poems
Penned by clever poets who
Don’t need to use a rhyme.

Don’t take our fields away from us
You don’t know what they mean to us.
We've worked this land and walk around
These fields that mean so much to us.
Our sweat and tears and sometime blood
Soaked deep into this fertile soil

It shares our very DNA, like dinosaurs and oil.
It fills our hearts and heads with green
It’s home no matter where we’ve been.
A refuge from life’s daily rush
Please don’t take our fields from us.
Our children jump in the muddy puddles
Dogs meet their friends in barky huddles
The clarity on a star filled night
The quiet that fits just right.
Don’t take all of these things away
It’s our backyard, that old cliché,
This field where our grandfolk played
Where our memories were made
Don’t take these fields from us
You don't know what they mean to us.

There are two types of gentlemen
Which category do you fall in?
The type who always appears calm or
The ones who always exude charm?
Some put knightly valour first
And seek to quench their driven thirst.
Others value honour most
They’re not unknown to selfish boasts.
Both have their virtues and their strengths,
Both have their foibles and their flaws,
Both are consistent in their beliefs
Especially when they clash with yours.
Then charade drops, pretence discarded
Claws and spite are now revealed
Under those urbane facades
A single-minded swine’s concealed.
There is another kind I’ve known
Who does not fight for favour
And I believe amongst this type
We may yet find our saviour.
The key word here, I believe,
If I could be sentimental,
Is not toxic masculinity
But is, instead, just Gentle.

I worry that my life will end
When I have nothing left to say
I’m worried that my lake’s in drought
And getting emptier day by day
I’m lost for words and new ideas
I need a prompt or gentle prodding
My powder is damp, I’ve lost the
Thread, I am an empty bobbin.
My tapestry fades and frays
My canvas's need repainting
I worry that I spend my time
Just procrastinating.
I’m worried that there is no more
An echo in a forsaken chapel
A wind that howls in hollow halls
Rustling the thoughts with which I grapple.
So I’ll write the disquiet down
Put its’ knives out of harm’s way
Trap them here so I can try to
Go on living day by day.

Off to the daily grind
Sucking blood keeps me alive
Death, where is thy sting?
Every night’s the same old thing.
Feels like an eternity
Same routine living differently
Daily chores are still chores
Alive or dead we still have flaws.
Undead struggle to move on
Can afterlife be improved upon?
Could there be something more?
Anything, beside this endless bore.
Lifeless bodies lie around
Calloused hearts make no sound
Calling for a steak to end it all
Just deserts the ghoul’s downfall.
Don’t let the buggers grind you down
Don’t drink the blood or wear that crown
Rejoin the living human race
A vampires life is just bad taste.

Hedgerows rustle furiously
Branches sway alarmingly
Leaves scuttle across the naked field
Racing the clouds fearfully.
Birds have flown somewhere calmer
While furry creatures burrow deeper
Stringy saplings bend and yield
Troubled skies await the thunder.
A distant banshee howling
Unwanted blast unsettling
Cold-fronts shame revealed
The air itself hyperventilating.
The pinball is in frantic play
Amid natures raw display
A chaos jar unsealed
The storm is underway.

I’ve given up rhyming for lent
I’m just writing prose for a while.
No more racking my brains
Going nuts and insane
If I fail you can put me on trial.
Damn it I messed up that verse
And this one is going to be worse
The rhymes just keep flowing
I don’t know what I’m doing
This poem needs to go in reverse.
My good intentions fell short
This isn’t the poem I sought
At least I have tried
At least nobody died
Not even the demons I fought.

The footpaths over English soil
Meander through the years
To the church or to the pub

For comradeship or beer.
Soon these fields may be no more
Given over to new homes
And paths that we have walked for years
Will soon be set in stone.
At the moment there is nature
And bird song in the Trees
But soon two hundred cars could come
And fill this space with ease.
Many people shoehorned into
Fields that once held cattle
The wildlife will be chased away;
They always lose the battle.
The views that stretched up to the hills
The food that used to grow here
The oxygen we used to breathe
Will soon be all enclosed here.
The footpaths that are drawn on maps
Don’t show the inspiration
That walking in these fields gave
This poet’s imagination.

And the park where I walk.
My paper and pen
Is my phone in the dark.
Following tails
Gives me tales to write
Which I pen on my own

When I walk late at night.
Fresh air and rain
Are the coffee I drink.
A slow steady gait
Gives me space to think,
Watching the change as
the seasons revolve.
I watch the page fill
As the writing evolves.
I circle the crops as
They’re sown and grow,
I dodge the tractors
That harvest then go.
They leave their marks
In the field where I walk.
I leave mine here
For the gods to mock.

All hail the sun, above our skies,
Celestial orb of fire!
Magical ball of enveloping warmth,
Our planet’s funeral pyre.
Beloved of priests and scientists too
For conflicting yet similar reasons.
Probed cautiously by our Icarus minds
The master of all of our seasons.
Lighting our journey through infinite space, Guiding us and also guarding
From the threatening meteorites,
Leading but also safeguarding.
As we corkscrew haphazardly we clutch
At the carelessly discarded power,
Learning to use what heaven provides
Now in our needful hour.

My night time walk around the park
Is dark and often cold.
I put lights on the dogs so I can see
They’re near me and haven't wandered off.
Sometimes the walks feel like a chore
Bit of a bore but it's good for me.
Though it’s cold and I forget to wear my gloves
It’s all for love and a chance to see the moon.
Sometimes one will find an enormous stick
Heavy, thick, it thumps into my legs.
Or they will find a smelly thing to eat
Disgusting treat I know they’ll throw up later.
But we all get a precious chance to think
Keeps us from the brink and falling over.
Round we go while my fingers freeze
I do believe it stops me getting older.

See that bird?
I’m gonna catch it
Off like a cannonball
Nearly – drat it!
They’re not like a ball
When you throw it, it stays
Why do the birdies
Always fly away?

Where will I be, thirty years from now
I used to ask myself, time to time
I’d imagine all sorts of nonsense
Nothing that seems familiar
To the life that is now mine.
I had hopes, fears and ideas
But I was wrestling a thing wilier
Than my narrow concepts.
Thirty years passed quicker than expected
Now I contemplate thirty more
There are many places I could be
Some where I wouldn’t want to be
And my conviction is no longer sure.
Each moment grows more precious
Every connection is more delicious
To savour as time passes;
Aging makes us thirsty.

As I sit down to write on a Tuesday
I wonder where the whole day has gone
Half of the day felt like a Thursday
I even found myself writing it wrong.
Tuesdays feel part of an infernal machine
A chimaera in a state of mercurial flux
Two gods of war, Norse Tiws, Roman Mars,
Throw tantrums while deep in their cups
We, more like Hanuman, trying to be strong
Work hard with devotion and grace.
We can all strive to be Tuesday child
The right day but in the wrong place.

Monday as quiet as a crash,
A dream befuddled by the dawn
An unwelcome ice bath challenge
And a fortune cookie torn.
The slap that clears your head
But lets you draw breath,
The fuel gauge light that
Shows how much is left.
The clanging claymore
Of a trillion souls
Inhale, exhale, as a throng,
Worker ants with one goal.
You feel them as
A pressure on your spine
The weekly wakeup call
To earn a dime.
Monday’s one day to get through
But also a chance, like the others,
To take this gift given
From all our mothers.
The moon day must follow the sun
That leads us, if we dare.
Turn our faces to the week
And prove they’re much more than fair.

Sunday morning, take a rest.
As the new week starts,
Take some time to ground yourself.
Life is not a headlong rush
From one chore to another.
Life needs some time to find itself.
There are six other days
In your busy week,
Time off is good for your health.
Take time to be bonny,
Blyth, good and gay;
Look after yourself on the Sabbath day.

Saturday is a list of jobs
You need to do at home
The weekly shop, the hoovering
The grass that must be mown.
We used to go to matinees
Now the kids play on PC's
Our folks would go to matches
So much time was free.
I steal a moment here and there
To write some random words
But new jobs, dropping cowpats,
Seem to come in herds.
There are daffodils on hillsides
That need a poet’s gaze
But I’m spring cleaning in the house
Lost in the ironing maze
Saturdays, I tell my sons,
Can be quite unforgiving,
Especially for those of us
Who work hard for a living.

It's Friday at last
It’s Friday at least
What does that mean
To a poet like me?
More time to write
More time to think
Or more distractions
From the work of the week
Nine to five toil
Is blessed relief
From having to think
And have self belief
But Friday is a tonic
When those all around you
Reach the weekend
Let their joy surround you.
I’ll put down my phone
Maybe start living
Be more like Fridays child
Loving and giving.

Thursday morning, eight AM
Stuck behind the bus again
Trying to get the kids to school
In traffic, running low on fuel.
Thursday is the longest day
With extra meetings that delay
And fill us full of sorrow, but
The weekend starts tomorrow.
We work hard to get things done
Clearing in-trays one by one
Reading emails, video calls
Thursday’s kick us in the balls.
Driving home at half past six
Getting the same traffic fix
Unlike Thursday’s child I know
That I have not got far to go.

I dream of the summer
And sun on my skin
Instead of the dark
And the cold winter brings.
I dream of a beach
And my feet in the sea
Instead I’m in wellies
And my feet seem to freeze.
I dream of long evenings
Sipping a cool beer
Instead I’ve got cocoa
And you snuggled near.
I miss the summer
But you keep me warm
I do love the sun
But I love you much more.

Come, Sleep, and take me
Carry me away
Fold me in cotton sheets
To sounds of waves
Cushion me and cuddle me
Calm me completely
Gently stroke my cares smooth
Tension release me
Dunk me in deep darkness
Cosy and warm
Come, Sleep, and swaddle me
Until the dawn.

I’m not a poet like the poets of old,
You know the ones that I mean.
They weren’t distracted by YouTube and memes
They legally had opioid dreams.
I’m not a poet like old what’s-his-name
Who’s ever so popular now.
His work regularly gets thousands of likes
Though God only knows how.
I’m not a poet that fought the great war
Up to their necks in the loam.
I can only imagine what they went through
My battles are closer to home.
I’m not a poet, but once nor were they
They probably also wrote dross.
Filled baskets with sonnets and insipid verse
Searching for true poetry sauce.
I’m not a poet like I’d like to be
I simply don’t have the mind,
But I’m happy with some of the poems I write
And some of the comfort I find.

Don’t sing me lies in a love song
When my heart is longing for truth
Don’t sing me lies with those deceitful sighs
When my heart is losing its youth.
You found me in my deepest winter
Promising me a new dawn
For the year ahead dreams filled my head
Easing a heart that was worn.
You’ve used those lies on others
Don’t use them now on me
Each time you lie a part of me dies
Leave me alone with ennui.
Together we blossomed in springtime
Awoken from long winter nights
Your passionate sighs blew the dust from my eyes
Contentment was finally in sight.
Don’t pen your lies in your poems
You haven't the wisdom or skill
Don’t pen your lies as a poetry prize
When my hearts lost the last of its will
My ardour grew hotter all summer
Fuelled by your words of desire
Your whispered wooing, my resolves undoing
My vanity thrown on the pyre.
Don’t write your lies in a letter
Don’t write of your deep despair
Don't talk of your debt or of your deep regret
To a heart that’s beyond repair.
Here I am lost in winter when
Autumn should bathe me in gold
My year was cut quick by your failing trick
Like the year my heart has turned cold.
So don’t sing your lies in a love song
And don’t write your lies in a book
Don’t paint me foolish for having a pure wish
And for having the courage to look.

I never wish for snow to fall
At Christmas,
I won’t take that bet.
I don’t need a silent night
Just sleigh bells,
And a string quartet.
At Christmas,
Play me cheesy tunes
And let me sleep all afternoon
Full to the brim
With Christmas fare
And swaddled with your love.
Just sleigh bells,
Like my ringing ears
The church chimes over frosty hills
And December’s icy air
Restoring my goodwill.
I never wish for snow to fall
As that is Christmas magic
Like the soft rhythmic ring
Of sleigh bells,
Unseen in the night
On Christmas eve
By starlight.

I’m taking a poetic break from reality
My bedside books are threatening to fall on me.
The pulp fiction is pissed that I’m not writing prose
But my poetry anthologies tell me anything goes
The nonfiction section snorts in distain
And my horror collection all feels the same
They’re threatening to maim.
A couple of romances (discretely hidden)
Are weeping because their hearts have been riven
Driven to despair, dear reader they grovel
And beg for support from my stack of crime novels
Hard-bitten detectives who’ve had it hard
Chew gloomy cheroots while fees are enlarged
Judgers chant “Guilty as charged”
“Put down that tablet, read us instead!”
Cry Shakespeare and Chaucer from under the bed
So I’m taking a break for my mental stability
Because this literature is slowly killing me!

Oh Baubles!
Hiding, silent, beneath the tree
The bane of baubles lurks
Waiting for the moment when
Her claws can do their work.
Disdainful of their glitteryness
Hungry for their shattering
Coiled ready, poised to pounce
Bows and bouquets scattering.
Heedless of the awful crash
Careless of the shards
Revelling in the fallen pine
And shredded Christmas cards.
Eviscerating toys and tinsel
Scratching the yule log
Curled up sleeping innocently;
Blame it on the dog.

Not every day can be a poem
Some are just not framed that way
The words you want to say get lost
In the hubbub of the day.
Or your mind’s a blank, a desert
Where no idea can grow
But that silence has a beauty
Revealing all that words don’t show.
Unburdening your foliage, let
The leaves fall where they may
On the days your mind’s a winter
Doing nothing is OK.
Not every day needs a poem
Some just need a steady hand
On the tiller, steering through
Life’s hazards small and grand.
Sometimes we don’t want to see
Another stanza, word, or letter
When it can become too painful
Being just a poor typesetter.
Trying to capture the sublime
With the petty words we say
So now and then I just absorb
And doing nothing is OK.

All I need is peace and love.
Some quiet and a big warm hug.
A place where I can shut the door,
And share a duvet, deep and snug.
All I need is calm and care,
A smooth sea and gentle air.
A safe harbour from the storm,
And knowing that you’re there.
Just sweet stillness and fondness,
A heart that let’s mine be free,
Where we can commune alone.
All I need is you and me.

I don’t understand particle physics,
Quantum mechanics, and most mathematics.
I can’t get my head around complex philosophy
I’m just a human with too much stuff thrown at me.
I wish I had time to take it all in,
To ponder life’s questions, where would I begin?
Poems like this are lamenting the fact
That I’m just wise enough to know what I lack.

I should never have tried bathing a cat.
I should’ve just left her where she was sat.
Now the water is red with the blood of the fool,
Who thought a clean kitty would be ever so cool.
I’m not the guy that you’d think was a biker,
And, if I’m honest, I didn’t think it either.
But I passed the test with tears, sweat and blood.
Motorcycles are heavy. My bike was called ‘Thud’.
A soft-play, they say, is a safe place for children,
With padding all over so the kiddies can run.
I tried running too, in that safe kiddie zone,
Fell smack on my arse and broke my tail bone.
The rock of Gibraltar is a great place to see,
And the apes that live there seem so friendly.
I think you can guess where I’m going with this:
The apes of Gibraltar don’t care where they piss.
I once met a lamb that was missing its mother,
So tried to reunite them. I shouldn’t have bothered.

I herded the damn thing, such an unselfish act,
Then tripped on a rock and my rib was cracked.
These are just a few of my life’s little errors,
That gave me bruises and cuts and night terrors.
I wish I could say that I’ve learned a lesson,
But I haven’t, so this is my therapy session.

She moves so fast, just like a blur,
It makes me feel in awe of her.
I move so slow, more like a snail,
Or maybe like a washed up whale.
She’s like a star, shining so bright,
Burns images into my sight.
I’m like dark matter, never seen,
Filling the spaces in-between.
Her power crackles like a fire,
Her calm command fuels my desire.
I am the struggling acolyte,
Wrestling emotions she excites.
I try to capture her completely,
With motion capture technology,
In doing so I’d lose it all:
I’d never catch her perfect soul.

A mile away there lives a man
I’ve never met before.
I don't know much about him
Other than we are at war.
If he lived a mile the other way
He wouldn't matter to me
But borderlines can alter minds
So what will be will be.
Just next door my neighbour
Whom I’ve known for many years
Mourns the loss of relatives
And cries bitter tears.
He crossed the valley long ago
While his wider family stayed
Before some leaders far away
Betrayed our naiveté.
A mile that way is a town
I can no longer to go there
Although the breeze that shakes my trees
Is also known to blow there.
I wonder if they look this way
When they’re not taking shelter?
I wonder if they’d wish me dead
Or dream of something better?
A mile here or there and
You would see much difference.
The people look and have the same
Mix of smarts and ignorance.
They farm the same soil we do
We both have the same view
We throw our bombs at them
And they bomb us black and blue.

When the squirrels in your head
Seem to have lost their nuts
And going crazy in your brain
Coping will take guts.
When you’re pulling your hair out
And no one seems to care
And the squirrels aren’t helping
Just by being there,
Remember to tell them
“Get back in your cages!”
Shout at those squirrels;
They can’t stand rages.
Squirrels and mind rodents
Need a firm steady hand
I’ve got plenty too
So I understand.

I walk down the street
Alone in a crowd
All walking together
With barely a sound.
We stop at the corner
And stand in the road
Unmindful of traffic
The road has been closed.
Here at the junction
A memorial stands
To the memory of souls
Who died in distant lands.
We lay our wreaths
And we all bow our heads
And we keep the silence
To acknowledge the dead.
After a while they
Read out the names
Conjuring images
Of distant campaigns.
There are far too many
For such a small little town
The street must’ve been

Empty with so few left around.
And quiet, and still,
Although life carried on
In the post-conflict world
Once the war had been won.
I walk down the street
Near the new shopping centre
I am here to pay tribute:
I have come to remember

A head full of sleepiness, eyelids are leaden,
An ambient noise in your ears, silence deafens.
Breathe slow to inhale the scent of darkness,
Exhaling a wish with a daggers sharpness.
When eyelashes meet there are flashes and sparks,
The throb of synapses lighting the dark.
Dreams being born before the main feature,
A choice for yourself, your id, or for neither?
The silent noises now make themselves known,
Without you noticing they’ve steadily grown.
But still soft enough to be drowned by a breeze,
The gentlest sigh as the world takes it ease.
Slowing, settling, the rhythm within.
Each thud is subdued, the heart sings its hymn.
A lullaby to every cell of your being.
Subconscious will care for you, while you are sleeping.

The adults build weapons
And the adults fly planes.
They plant IEDs
And play nasty games.
Do adults think about
The injuries they cause,
Or the terrified children
Who can’t go outdoors?
The adults hold grudges,
They also hold power
They taunt their enemies@
They sulk and glower.
The adults keep score
Of each small victory.
The children are collateral,
A footnote in history.
Adults like winning
They won’t compromise.
They say “We won’t hurt you”
But they are telling lies.
The adults will blow up
Your school to get even.
The children are silent
And all up in heaven.

When winter comes I need a cave
Somewhere to hibernate in.
A place I can sleep, rest, paws
Cleansing and exfoliating
Through the year I’ve bearly stopped
Eating fish and nuts and berries
Now the land’s turned polar here
I’ll sleep away my worries.
You might miss my grizzly face
Or welcome a bit less growling
But I would rather take a nap
Than prowl around here howling.
So while I panda to myself
And take a little time out
Please bear with me patiently
I’m close to black- or brownout.
I know that I must do something
And snoozing always seems sublime
So I will take a winter break
Having some koala-ty time.
