Please don’t Pooh-pooh this parable
Spring makes my puns more bearable

In that nether time, when the clocks go back,
Do the chimes of thirteen make the witches attack?
While the full moon floats heavily on top of the clouds,
Illuminating on a whim what the devil allows.
Autumn mists seep from the rain soaked mud,
Hiding what needs hiding and chilling the blood.
Turning silver and translucent when the moment is best,
Hanging shrouded and heavy when put to the test.
It is only an hour, and time is an abstract,
So why do we feel each second like a cat scratch?
Claws on a blackboard and a threatening hiss,
This isn’t the night to be making a wish.
When we give extra time to a late autumn night,
We offer ourselves to the darkest of frights.

Just ignore this writing, it’s not supposed to be here.
It’s just saving a place, for something more inviting.
Waiting for it to appear, I needed to fill the space,
With something less taxing, something less severe.
I might have to erase, or just start extracting,
‘Til I’ve a new one to share, Or maybe a brace.
This is just place holding: I’ve no soul to bare.
There’s nought to embrace, my muse is hiding.
I know good poems are rare, and this isn’t a race.
Please ignore my rambling, it shouldn’t be here.

Brought to the block, we stand and stare
Awaiting the chop for what we share.
The pen can cut you like a knife
It’s might surpasses any swords
Wielded by my clumsy hands
I cannot find the words.
We mitigate our motives
Because reasons are excuses
Whittle down the angry hours
Put them to better uses.
Must we bleed by making points?
Must there be pain and anguish?
Why should we suffer for our art
When art itself is selfish?
I feel the sting of sharp steel
I taste the miscast mettle
I turn my face away from the
Reverse side of the medal.
To this block I offer my neck
I stuck it out for you to wreck.
I use my pen one final time
Then rest upon the guillotine.

What will you take with you when you are buried?
My mother took a Kit Kat, my father his medals
Not much is left of either but I hope it was a comfort
Taking solace to the ground, there to gently settle.
Pharaohs took replicas of all their worldly chattels
Everything that they might need for their future travels
Sealed for eternity, or until it was all stolen
The curse is empty whispers; their seal knots unravelled.
Warlords took their enemies, heroes took their laurels
Vikings took their longboats, bog men took their shackles
Victorians in shrouds erected angels at their feet
Soldiers piled with their mates at the scenes of battles.
What will I take with me when I’m laid to rest?
Scattered with the ashes of me in my Sunday best?
It won’t be clever words, I’ll leave all of those behind
But I will take all the love with which I have been blessed.

Which is the worst poem I’ve ever written?
Was it the one about the disabled kitten?
Or maybe the one where I went on and on,
About nothing particularly cheerful.
I've written some dross that didn’t quite rhyme,
I seem to cover the same themes all the time.
I trip over the words when I read them out loud,
And I pack in a plethora of syllable.
Perhaps I didn’t quite hit the nail on the head?
Or is that how it feels when the poem is read?
Does this talk of nailing make you so cross,
That you just want to give me an earful?
I’ve got my own list of ones that are stinkers.
Writings I fear will offend all freethinkers.
Ones that use two words when one will do,
Rereading them just makes me tearful.
But, to me, and I am my own fairest judge,
The worst that I find when I delve in the sludge,
Are the unfinished poems that promised so much,
But then, I’m hardly impartial.

Here’s a quick look at tomorrow’s news:
Continued strife between Arabs and Jews.
Political parties all blaming each other,
School kids being taught how to take cover.
An earthquake flattens a small remote town,
The kidnap victims have still not been found.
The invasion is bogged down in the snow,
The unions are calling for wages to grow.
The weather is out of control it would seem,
A poor country elects a hard-line regime.
A gunman is still on the loose in the city.
A businessman lies to an oversight committee.
Finally a round up of the local crime.
The news hasn't changed much in my lifetime.

A young man asked me if I was OK
I chuckled but didn’t know quite what to say
I’m lucky to still be around here today
So I guess that should classify as being OK
He didn’t believe me and pressed for some more
My nervous smile said that I wasn’t quite sure
And I wondered if I ought to show him the door
Or share with him my thoughts and stories galore.
Is it called oversharing, what kids do these days?
Loneliness loosens lips I’ve heard some folks say
But me, well I wasn’t always so old and grey
And the kid inside sometimes comes out to play.

I lie awake at night cursing the fools,
That brought all of this to our door.
And when I sleep I dream about how,
One day I’ll even the score.
The cold light of day sobers me up,
Reality bites me once more.
I smile for my enemies , wearing a mask,
Because one day I’ll even the score.
Hate is stew that boils for hours,
Seasoned with spices galore.
Guaranteed to stick in the throat,
When served up to even the score.
The seething resentment, acidic bile,
Burns me ‘til I lose all control.
My aim is to even the score but I find,
In the end I just score an own goal.

I asked an old man, “How old do you feel?”
He laughed and replied “The minds age isn’t real.
Although I am stiff and creak as I kneel
You’re only as old as the person you feel”.
I wasn’t convinced so I asked “Aren’t you tired?”
Chuckling he said “Yes, but I haven’t expired.
Exhaustion’s the reward of being desired,
And I am refreshed by the children I’ve sired”.
“But your body” I cried, “Don’t you fear atrophy?
Do you seek replacements for elbows and knees?”
He smiled and replied “They mean nothing to me.
Life’s here for the living, not the legacy”.

As an old sailor, I remember,
The curve of the horizon on a placid sea.
As a novice flat earther i find,
that memory is conflicting to me.
Because I see archaeologists digging,
Through bone laden layers of strata,
But do my flat earth beliefs allow,
For stuff under the terra-firma?
And on star filled nights I walk,
Troubled by the heavens above.
My limited dimensional dogma,
Means they’re thoughts I’m wary of.
For though i can see them revolving,
And they all appear to be round,
A flat earther like me must question,
Whether that also applies to the ground.

I sit here and ponder the moss on the floor
Everything else has been pondered before
By pondering I’m really just wasting time
Squandering moments both yours and mine.
I uselessly wonder if the moss ponders me
Sat still and verdant, outwardly serenely
It’s concept of purpose must be alien
As its life passes by, then begins again.
How did it get here, was it kicked from a roof?
Did a disgruntled lyricist use it as proof
That beauty and meaning don’t require truth
And that gathering moss is the ruin of youth.

Potatoes like me, we grow underground
We have eyes to see but don't make a sound
We’re not celebrated until we are peeled
Tossed in a salad, our insides revealed.
Potatoes like me, and most other tubers
Don’t want to be boiled or roasted by humans
Our lives shouldn’t end up mashed on a plate
Show some compassion for what you just ate.
Potatoes like me deserve some respect
But short, round and bald, it’s not what you get
Dress me up smartly or admire my jacket
Don’t slice me up finely and put me in a packet.
Potatoes like me prefer watching TV
We don’t need fine dining, no fricassee
Go play with your dumplings, just leave me be
Don’t put on the menu a potato like me.

At midnight by phonelight,
You’ll find me here.
Drinking and thinking and well aware,
How somethings are harder than others.
It’s midnight and I might,
Be here for awhile.
Rhyming and trying to find a style.
But just out of reach it hovers.
It’s midnight and just right,
To close my eyes,
Resting, digesting my lows and highs.
Reliving the winters and summers.
At midnight I’ll recite,
My hard-won prose.
Growing and evolving, my banner arose:
Nailed to the mast are my colours.

My life is picking up piles of clothes
And carrying them down to the laundry
When I look back from that big washing stack
I see all that I’ve dropped behind me.
I tried to pick up every garment
From the washing piles left by the tykes

Dropped everywhere on the floor, on the stair
One of my favourite dislikes.
My life needs a new laundry basket
Or some other plan to get past it
Maybe training the kids, just like Pavlov did
Before I’m laid out in my casket.
Life, I believe, is too short for chores
Making us feel discontent
So I’ll pick up the washing and stuff it all in
Until I can afford servants.

Cats eyes, they say, can see in the night.
They can see it all, wrong or right.
Dogs on the other hand see with the nose,
Their eyes only see black and white.
Some people can only see their own rage,
Stuck rigidly to their own holy page.
They see only differences and so, cling
To the doctrines of the war that they wage.
Cats are the hunters, stalking their prey.
Silently creeping, then making their play.
Dogs are the chasers, swift as the wind,
Relentless, noisy, they won't back away.
Some people are too quick with their teeth
Their claws are ready to be unsheathed.
Sharp with their tongue or their knives.
Burning with a deep hatred beneath.
Both cats and dog can share the same home.
Living together and they all get along.
Yet, with our neighbours, we readily fight
Why do we get it so wrong?

Inside my head are boxes crammed,
With thoughts I try to keep contained.
Some are nailed, some are jammed,
Others locks are highly strained.
A few hold candles, all unburned,
Flames controlled perhaps by fears,
Perhaps because my love was spurned.
Some are full of uncried tears.
There are some boxes full of air,
Captured traces of perfume,
Of scents that I now cannot bear.
Mere shadows of the rarest bloom.
I keep these boxes buried deep,
So they aren’t opened by mistake.
And yet I fear their contents seep,
Into my thoughts when I’m awake.
But also there are lots of crates,
Full to the brim with pure delights,
The memories of blissful dates,
And euphoric nights.
These I cherish and rummage through,
Lose sweet hours replaying times,
When life was young and love was new,
The finest food and vintage wines.
These boxes don’t need lids or locks,
And overflow chaotically,
Fill my heart and never stops,
Cheering me enormously.

This was going to be a five minute poem
Written quickly without too much thought
But now it has been several hours
And I’ve written much less than I ought.
I wasn’t looking to pen passionate prose
I just wanted to quip a quick ditty
I hadn’t even thought of a theme
And a rudderless rhyme isn’t pretty.
Now I’m lost for a half decent ending
For a coup that’ll finish the piece
But the clocks running out on this poem
So I’ll leave it here as an esquisse.

In the dark
I’m walking in the dark
Following a shadow
Underneath the stars
In a country meadow
Stretching out the moments
Because busy lives are short
Listening to the traffic
That intrudes upon my thoughts.
I can see the streetlights
Smell the fresh ploughed soil
walking in the darkness
I feel myself uncoil.
Any peace is transient
Likewise stress can come and go
I snatch comfort where I can
And maintain the status quo.

Searching the scene of the crime,
Looking for evidence of our affair.
Here is a heart that's in pieces and,
Your fingerprints are everywhere.
There’s trace left behind carelessly,
That proves that you were around.
There’s circumstantial indicators,
Of a love smashed all over the ground.
You may have had a watertight story,
Or an alibi you think can’t be broken.
But my logical mind will unravel,
All the lies that your lips have spoken.
Methodically I’ll piece it together,
All the facts of this tragic case.
In the hope I gain the conviction,
And a closure that I can embrace.

Soft light and warmth: you writhe in the gore
Eating the rot you grow wings yet want more
Disturbed from the corpse you rise as a swarm
You’re drawn to excreta preferably still warm
Crapulous carefree corpulent existence
Blown by the breeze of your whims - a pretense
Your fatuous flitting defines your demise
Your engorged body watched with hungry eyes
Captured in chrysalis, spun around by those legs
You feel your life draining, sucked out as you beg
Hanging suspended you feel the web twitch
A swifter death is your futile last wish.

I’m sitting, word knitting, but I don’t have a pattern.
The wool in my head means I’m not sure what happens.
I use these analogies instead of real needles,
And hope they articulate just how it feels.
This row was a pain that I had to redo.
These stitches in blue are still under review.
There’s a bit at the back that’s started unravelling,
And the neon and gold bits are simply dazzling.
Ribbing and purling and cable and birds eye,
All intermingled, a real knitter would cry.
I’m losing the tread of where this was going,
But at least all the loose bits inside aren’t showing.
The hemming and harring will never get done,
And if I’m not careful more stitches will run.
I’ve not even thought about buttons and bobbles,
I’ve mixed up enough when making up morals
I’m sad for the sheep whose fine fleece was shorn,
To end up with this mess and all out of yarn.

Rainbows look beautiful
Up in the sky
Between the rain and the sunshine
The empyrean eulogy
I’ve never seen them fairly captured
By photographer or painter
Their beauty is ephemeral
And not meant to linger.
A gift of creation
In radiant hues
Familiar, predictable
Surprising and new.
Our childhood pictures
And folklore ramblings
Skirting the edges
Of beatific mythology.
Emblazoned across our familiar aerosphere
Each one a new revelation
A delight for our reborn infantile eyes
Our favourite familiar formation.
We reach for it and search for its ends
Enchanted despite ourselves
If just for a moment, knowing that
Rainbows are fleeting, just like ourselves.
It’ll soon be gone
The light will change or more rain will fall
And we will go on without it
But we know that someday one will reappear
So perhaps we can too, in some distant year.

People don’t often agree
Over borders or poetry.
Are we right to fight?
I don’t think we are.
I don’t care if you disagree.
Because maybe by agreeing to fight
over what one person wrote as was their wont
We’re taking a stand
In that virtual fantasy online land.
I won’t say I think I’m better
Nor will I tell you how bad I think you are
I won’t type it or private message you.
I keep that poison in me
I use it as my ink
Blowing out clouds of it to hide myself
Like a bird in a hedge at night
You'll hear me chattering under my breath
And rustling my words of death.
Make Love not war
A difficult man once said.
I’m trying
To keep these knives inside my head.

Poets are like chicken farmers
Tending to their flock
Picking out which egg to break
And who ends up on the block.
Poets are like acrobats
Showing off their skill
Practising in private
Unbalanced and unwell
Poets are like chickens
Pecking in the dirt
Trying to find some nourishment
From chicken feed and hurt
Poets are the circus clowns
Made-up to look their best
A sideshow for the circus crowd
A role which they detest
Poets are the eggs we eat
With tough yet brittle shells
Walk on them and you will find
Their egos break as well.
Poets are the circus tent
The audience are hens
From up above we look at them
Through our distorted lens.

When the bombs have stopped falling
We can send them all back
To their home in the mountains
that our allies attacked.
They can pick up the pieces
That our bombs blew apart
They can rebuild their houses

But not their broken hearts.
When we’ve restored the peace
And we’ve rebuilt some roads
We can sell them some weapons
From our stock that got old.
They don’t need care homes
Or any nursery schools
The kids crushed or drowned
And the old are just bones.
So we’ll take refugees in
For a while at least
So our conscience is clear
When the fighting has ceased.
But the bombs are still falling
And there’s no sign of peace
Lives are still being shattered
From afar with such ease.

When I get stuck in a poem
I just move along to the next
Leaving the unfinished in limbo
Feeling a little bit vexed.
When I reopen the notebook
And flip to a page that is blank
I pass by the poetry scrapyard
I pass the rhyming sperm bank.
Sometimes one gets my attention
I see something that could still be saved
Attempting poetic surgery
My butchery is almost depraved.
Nothing you write is unworthy
None of it’s wasted completely
Even if some is too earthy
An edit or two will help greatly.

Why is it you want to befriended me on Facebook?
Do you just want access to my private friend group?
Are you going to spam me with unwanted ads
For the trash that you’re selling or the latest fad?
Or are you trying to steal my identity
I think there’s too many with just the one of me.
And my bank account’s empty, us poets are poor
Poems are pyrite but I can always write more.
If I check out your page will I like what I see
Is it you in your skivvies or pictures of trees?
Are you pushing a diet too good to be real
Or AI images of your fantasy meals?
Is your profile locked down and inaccessible
Is it shiny and new, is it too good to be true?
Are you a celebrity who’s misspelt their name?
I’ve seen so many I’m getting wise to that game.
But maybe you asked me because you like my verse
I do hope it’s that and not something much worse
I’ve made friends on here from all over the world
I’d love to add you if you know the magic word.

There are different types of poets I’ve found
Especially since the internet’s been around
With differing styles and various voices
Some light-hearted and others profound.
Some write at length about their distress
Pouring their hearts into every syllable
Flaying themselves to get some relief
Drowning us all with a flood almost biblical.
Some prefer spouting streams of consciousness
Long rhyming diatribes; their banners unfurled
Pouring acid bathwater over their readers
Lamenting, berating - a bagpipes bass skirl
There are others who just like brevity
Who like breaking rules for the levity
Who don’t give a damn for longevity
And have no time for poetic pregnancy.
Free-versers just write however they want
For as long as they feel they want it to be
No rhyme punctuation or device needed
Creating cacophony and literary anarchy
There are those who adhere to strict form
Counting the beats and timing the rhythm
Preferring the schemes of bygone times
Each finished couplet being a firm lesson.
Me? I prefer poetry nudism
Letting it hang out, all on display
It may not always be pretty
But it’s mine and to me its OK.
There’s something for everyone out there

And everyone has something to share.

List of things to take with you to University.
I’ve made you a list of things to take with you
When you embark on your next great adventure
It’s not the usual things like posters and pillows
And it’s not wacky stuff like Daleks or dentures.
I want you to take confidence in yourself
You’ve earned your place and you’ll do alright
I want you to take all the laughter we share
So it’s there if you need it late in the night.
I want you to take lots of laundry detergent
Your common sense and your sense of caution
I want you to take both your parents, just kidding
But know that we’ll visit en-masse very often.
I’ve packed enough food to last you a month
Or for a few days if your flatmates are hungry
There’s a box full of hugs and studenty rugs
And homemade biscuits, deliciously crumbly.
Most of all I want you to take all our love
We’re with you in spirit and we’re not far away
You’re taking our pride if you want it or not
And were here if you need us, anytime night or day.

Icarus flew and was feeling the heat
Isn't it typical of boys of his age?
Being so reckless, knowing better.
Don’t blame the wings he was given
Little birds were telling him what can be done
But those birds don’t go near the sun.
Icarus is dead and broken now
And yet achieved immortality
Or at least a certain notoriety.
But who gave him those ideas, those wings?
Arrest Daedalus whose own impractical dreams
Like ours and Icarus, lie shattered.
They should have known better
When they swore that they were sane
Freedom to soar was their god given right.
We normalise flying in our defence
So blame society or the family
Just don’t blame the wings.

What stands in our way
Is not hard to define
It’s the deserts and oceans
And mountains we can’t climb.
We strive to get over
Each obstacle we find
Yet the toughest that we face
Are the ones in our minds.
What stands in our way

What must be overcome
Maybe our painful frailty
Or ghosts of things we’ve done
Perhaps we are repeating
Mistakes we’ve made before
The obstacles that we face
Won’t defeat us anymore.
What stands in our way
It isn’t in our past
It’s the future come what may
But isn’t going to last.
It will flash by us so fast
And somehow that’s okay
Whatever obstacles we face
That becomes the way.

What is the name for the ripples in the sand
In the shallow water near the beach?
What is the name for the insubstantial cloud
That hovers overhead just out of reach?
What is the word for the feeling that you get
When a sunset seems to touch your very soul?
Is there a phrase for when your mind is blank
And the words you want to say you can’t cajole?
Hidden in the lexicon could a higher mind
Pick a better class of words to say or use?
I will just have to make do with simpler things
To express my simple heart and “I love you’s”.

In my cellar I’ve collected
Carefully selected
Vintages from everywhere
That I keep bottled up.
I descend into that room
Sniff about amid the gloom
Dust off a few old labels
And smile at the memories
Perhaps I’ll take a bottle down
With a corkscrew in my hand
Offer you a little taste
With a knowing smile
But if I do, watch what I say
You might need to call the AA
One sip is never enough
And soon this waggons crashing
I can’t put the cork back in
The bottle, once I begin
I have to let it flow until
The whole damn thing is empty.
Words flow like a waterfall
Over the cliff I throw them all
They run through the grate
In my cellar floor.
If I invite you to a tasting
Understand the test you're facing
Moderation and control
Lest we drown this poets soul.

The song I can’t sing.
I’m not a great composer
I’ve not got a great voice
Nor can I play an instrument
It’s lack of skill not choice.
My rhythm is embarrassing
I can not hold a tune
My whistling just blows
And I cannot even croon.
But all around me music floats
It permeates my soul
An all enthusing symphony
That links and makes us whole
I look and see it everywhere
It’s right in front of me
You’re all the score that fills my life
The chords that strike me free.

When I look back
At the poems I wrote
What must be a whole year ago
Some I’m quite pleased with
Some are alright
Some are only so-so.
When the pen leaves the paper
Or the finger leaves the phone
Is the poem over if it gets left alone?
Should I add a coda
Or a dozen more stanzas?
Attack it like a tiger or a blitzkrieging panda
What I’m saying I guess
Is that I tried my best
And I’m learning as I go along
The main thing I’ve learnt
From this fountain of words
Is that sometimes they just come out wrong.

And you gave yours to me
A fair exchange like golden rings
I’m sure you will agree.
That exchange was just the start
The cornerstone we laid
The tower of love we’ve built stands tall
This fortress that we’ve made.
Every room we’ve furnished with
Reflections of devotion
Lined with joy and sweat and tears
Passion that’s unbroken
This citadel surround and protect
But is also insubstantial
For our love is not tied to one place
And cannot be dismantled.
The foundation laid so long ago
Upon which we are still building
Brings me everyday such joy

That my whole soul is singing.

We’re not as small as solar dust
We're sure not as big a planet
But we’re all lost in space
All gathered into one place
Pulled together by a cosmic magnet.
We are not as fast as a shaft of light
We don’t go so slow as a snail
But we’re all on this ride
For the rest of our lives
Which are measured on a quantum scale.
Our momentum is keeping us moving
Our potential becomes all kinetic
But there are other forces
That attract and divorce us
And make our lives so poetic.

The sun is sliding below the horizon
I feel the soft wind that is blowing the night in
And just before stars steal the earths heat
You smile at me and the day is complete.
The simplest of sighs can blissfully brighten
Your aura dispels the demons I’m fighting
With you on my team we’ll never be beat
Your love is the sugar that makes my life sweet
Loving you gives me the strength to keep writing
Reliving each poem is something I delight in
My muse and afflatus, my prize and my treat
These small rhymes of ardour are ones I’ll repeat

Imagine a world without burgers
No tasty stack piled high
No layers of cheeses and sauces
No meat to have with your fries.
Now imagine a world without TV
The way it was years ago
None of the channels to flick through
An absence of your favourite show
Picture a world without colour
Everything in shades of grey
You’d live in it because you had to
Missing what brightened your day.
Envision a world without music
No tunes either classical or pop
Nothing to hum or to dance to
As if God hit the button marked Stop.
Now imagine you took yourself from us
The way desperate folk sometime do
All of these verses would be real
That’s how we’d feel without you.

Sometimes when I’m walking
I can feel the world spinning

The rock we’re on revolving
and the core inside that's burning.
Although I’m only plodding
the world we're on is hurtling
Around a sun that keeps exploding
and its heat keeps us existing.
I can see to the horizon
But I feel the world expanding
On a walk with no direction
I could use an explanation
For the oxygen I’m wasting
With my idle speculation
About our final destination
When the evidence I’m gathering
Let’s me draw no firm conclusions
So I’ll walk as shadows growing
Hide my own petty illusions
I will find I’ve walked in circles
With no final resolution
To my internal revolution.

Do I walk my dog or does she walk me?
I choose the route and she leads the way.
She glances back sometimes to see if I’m there,
I point out our direction but she doesn’t care.
Maybe our walks have become too routine,
Maybe we just need to find a new scene,
Go somewhere exotic and damn the cost,
She’d do her own thing and I would get lost.
So we’re better here with our forest and bog,
Where she can walk me and I walk the dog.

I stopped all the dogs from barking
Their noise was just a nuisance
It’s not like they had anything to say
That didn’t sound like an accusation.
I ordered the birds to stop singing
When their chirping became too loud
I need quiet to hear myself think
And their nonsense is not allowed.
I silenced the kids and their music
They all should be seen but not heard
Instead they should listen to my song
Or the ones that their elders preferred.
One Day the world will be silent
With no voices raised in dissent
The population all kept in their place
And freedom of speech will be dead.

Being a man of science
I scoff at superstition
Even though saluting crows
Is now a firm tradition.
I can live quite normally
Under the laws of physics
But some primeval part of me
Needs cathedral visits
I know that space above me
Stretches in an endless void
I also hope that out there somewhere
Someone hears my voice.
The solar rays that warm me
Send a tingle down my spine
The unseen ghosts that haunt me
Are explainable but divine.
I embrace my irrationality
It's part of being human
In subatomic biology there’s
A metaphysical fusion.

I could be a pollinator
And fly from flower to flower
Measure out my years
Like the minutes of an hour.
Though life may seem short
If you quantify each moment
Every flower is a blessing
Each sip of nectar potent.
I will do this dance of joy
Showing others where to go
And I’ll build a hive of honey
Then be gone before it snows.

Everybody has their scars
And some of them are bleeding
Some are hidden by the bruises
From repeated beatings.
Some of us are boxers who will
wear their wounds with pride.
For others they’re a source of shame
That they would gladly hide.
Some people have both sorts
But don’t want to talk about it.
Other folk can’t hold it in
And find they have to shout it.
All of us have all this stuff
We carry around with us
But we can share the burden out
So it doesn’t kill us.

I walk and I work
And I wonder what else
I can find that’ll make me
Believe in myself.
I read and I write
And I fill in the gaps
That appear in my soul
As my confidence sags.
I fail and succeed
In the most random fashion
And neither’s affected
By apathy or passion.
So I sleep and I wake
And I fly or I fall
And I hope in the end
I’ll make sense of it all.

It’s too wet for poems
It's raining too hard
I can't work my phone
When there’s rain on the glass
I start a new line and
Then wipe off the droplets
But it’s raining so hard
I’ve lost track of the couplets
I guess I could write
Something deep about rain
But it’s such a downpour
I’ve been washed down a drain
At least I’m not using
A pencil and paper
My thoughts would be mushy
When I look at them later.

Several seagulls circling me
Hungrily hunting chips for tea
Frantically flapping one arm in the air
Peckishly pecking the pests do not care.
Squawky squabbling over their prey
Bullying bombers get in my way
Face full of fowl feathers I turn the air blue
Denied dinner the nasty sods poo.
Encased In car I can finally eat
Cold chilly chips aren’t much of a treat
Eagerly eyeballed I open the car door
The happy hunters eat chips from the floor.

There are new memories every day
Of the way I lived on this very date
Like five years ago at that big party
We got drunk and stayed up too late
Or way further back when I was lonely
And asked if there was someone to love
It was the first time I’d ever seen frozen
And frankly just once was enough.
Here’s pics of our wedding four years ago
The sun and the cake and how beautiful
You looked in that dress and in my arms
And we both felt that life was wonderful
Much further back there’s one of my exes
She blocked me so I can’t see her comments
I wrote her long messages from far away
And posted the most ridiculous sonnets
Three years ago I see I’m holding our baby
The smallest most precious thing ever

There’s not many entries from two years ago
Around when you went up to heaven.
Sometimes the absence of memories
Makes you recall things much sharper
Like the smell of your hair or your singing
Or the delicate sound of your laughter
Last years post was from a holiday
The kid and I visiting relatives
Growing so quickly and learning so fast
Leaving me no space to be negative
No time to reflect on the past times
From these reminders I take small sips
Look far back to when I had more hair
Or the game that gave me free poker chips
Now I’m just trying to make entries
To drown out the others that haunt me
Rebuilding the home that was fractured
And remember the lessons you taught me.
To laugh and to sing and to cherish
The life that goes on all around us
To make the most of each moment
Of love that this life allows us.

The leader and his generals
Pose outside the cathedral
Where a hundred of his enemies
Were vanquished.
Their final stand was meaningless
In this endless game of chess
The hundred schoolboys
Less than he had wished.
Make examples of your foes
Cut off your face to spite your nose
Tell the whole world that
You are fighting evil.
You’re not here for hearts and minds
It’s territory that you prize
Historically it’s worth it,
This upheaval.
In a month its all forgotten
But for bodies slowly rotting
In the city ruined
There’s no one to remember.
I hope the ghosts of those lost boys
Tear at your dreams, steal your joy
Until all you wish for
is your own surrender.

Your eyes met mine across a room
And melted me completely
A feeling that was old and new
Changing my life so sweetly.
Our eyes met in a holy place
When you met me at the altar
A look that vowed a love like ours
Could never fade or falter.
My eyes can find no better sight
Than all the joy you’ve shown me
And I will love you everyday
Like all the days you’ve known me.

There are many different types of poem
Different styles that you can try
Who’s to say which type is better
Find a fit that let’s you fly
Like the colours of a rainbow
Merge and blend your poets voice
Open hearts have more to say
And open minds have greater choice
Fill your canvas with your essence
Show your truth for all to see
Although some won’t get your vision
Sharing yourself takes bravery
Being you is not for others
It’s yourself you need to be
No apologies are needed
Life’s too short for bigotry.

Sneaking downstairs for a late night snack
I have to tiptoe or I’ll wake the cat
My eyes grow accustomed to the gloom
As I make my way through the living room
Then I’m in the kitchen and head for the fridge
I take a deep breath and muster my courage
Open the fridge door and, blinded by light,
The dogs, cat and children appear for a bite.
I wasn’t so sneaky or stealthy or quiet
At least, now they’re here, I’ll stick to my diet.

Drinking used to clear my head
Now meditation does instead
It might atone for pain I’ve caused
When you were mine and I was yours
The cruel things that I used to say
When anger led my heart astray
Lost in that darkness that obscures
When you were mine and I was yours
You saved yourself at my expense
Escape your only best defence
What memories my mind endures
When you were mine and I was yours
My metamorphosis from that beast
Allows this pain to be released
So with forgiveness and some time
I will be yours and you’ll be mine

Where is the well?
Where is the source?
Where is the spring
that freshens the horse?
Lost underground,
Stolen by drains,

Piped far away
to funereal strains.
Where is the spark?
Where is the flame?
Where’s the inferno
that raged without shame?
Smothered, neglected,
Denied the fuel,
Nothing but embers
Teasing and cruel.
Fire and water
Essential and precious
Both of them needed
To anoint and bless us.
To call forth our spirit
To inspire and ignite
Raise us to the struggle
Refresh and excite.

The canvas is ready
The brushes laid out
But the paints are unopened
So all is a blank
The statue encased
In the marble cocoon
Awaiting the chisel
And a reason to bloom.
Notebook neglected
Child unborn
Novel, prose, poetry
Genre is unknown.
The play is the thing
The thing that’s not done
There are no actors
There’s no Chekov’s gun.
An unfinished symphony
That hasn’t been started
The music in the ether
Has yet to be charted.
The tower is unbuilt
No cornerstone fitted
No dwelling, no home
No building permitted.
Lights, camera
but no action
The crew is on strike
Lost all direction.
This list is unfinished
And falls short of art
It can’t be completed
When it can’t even start.

The ancient landscape where we dwell
one that our ancestors knew so well
Was inherited from the dinosaurs
and echoed with their mighty roars
Now that great wilderness is tamed
Man’s selfish needs are to be blamed
Primeval forests turned to fields
Hunters now harvest what they yield
The wildlife is all tamed or trapped
and mountains lose their snowy caps
But dinosaurs can still be heard
They scream from cars and scare the birds
I hear them now wherever I am
Howling like their souls are damned
As a dark warning to us who take
What this planet cannot replace.
Will we be like those dinosaurs
killed off by some meteors?
Or will we cause our own destruction
through greed and lack of education?

Sat on the decking looking down to the road
Over grass that is brown and dying
The hedge full of nesting beer cans
And the cars that fly past sighing.
I think of the day when I’ll plant a tree
Over there, where the earth is not toxic
One that will grow sturdy and strong
Despite the occasional oil slick.
Years from now I will sit in its shade
In a garden I’ve nurtured and tended
Proud of the flora that I can pass on
And the nature that I’ll have defended.

I started writing poetry
as a mental exercise,
Writing down the crazy thoughts
That swam before my eyes.
Then I thought I’d share them
With my Facebook family
But having to perform each day
Has put a strain on me.
Soon I was writing just because
I needed to post more,
Searching for a good idea
I didn’t know what for
I joined groups to share my words
With other kindred souls
Reading others poems came
To be an improvement goal.
Groups with thousands posting
Soon became an maelstrom
My time was spent just reading
Poems instead of writing them.
Hobbies become obsessions
It affects my mental health
So I’m going back to writing
And every line is just myself.
If it doesn’t make me happy
how can it then please you?
If the lines are artificial can
the whole be something true?
I was even asking A.I.
If my work was any good
Seeking reassurance
But not sure if I should.
So it’s time to take some time
And re-find my inner rasp
Let the ideas germinate
Till they’re within my grasp
This might mean I’m posting less,
But please don't start to worry
My poetry cannot be forced
or be written in a hurry.

I’ll grant you three wishes
and guess what they are
You want to go travelling?
We will go in my car.
I’ll show you the places
That you’ve longed to see
The only drawback is
You'll see them with me.
Your second one’s easy
You wish for World Peace
I’ll get everyone talking
and soon war will cease.
But you may find that
this is a poisoned cup,
whenever you're near me
I just won’t shut up.
Now I know your last one
Then I’m gone with a Pop!
I’ll grant your last wish...

Facebook has now been around a while
It keeps all my witty posts neatly filed
Pictures of pets and places I’ve been to
Cars I’ve owned and the kids as they grew.
Once a day I’m reminded of these memories
And all my old posts are replayed to me
So much I’ve stored in its memory banks
Except for the days that are total blanks.
What was I doing? I can’t recall
Probably just lots of nothing at all
Nothing worth making a post about
Or was I on a ban? What was that about?!
Here’s a link I posted a few years ago
But now when I click it’s a no show
was it offensive, racist or rude?
There’s nothing to see so I have no clue.
I guess that’s why I’m doing this poetry
To fill up my timeline with things to read
So that if I begin to get elderly
Facebook can show me these memories.

What have I learnt today?
Nothing very much it seems
I keep making the same mistakes
Building on some broken dreams.
I’ve left undone my promises
And squandered petty hours
Doing chores and getting by
My motor set to Idle power.
My certainties were vanities
And cloistered self indulgence
My strengths were fiction
Flattered by my intelligence.
Taking stock may help me see
The road that let me to this point
And give me the sense to evaluate
Perhaps some clues I can exploit
As I stumble on with life
Playing this perpetual game
To try some options that are new
So the future may not be the same.

Don’t think there’s any rhyme or reason to this,
I’m spouting the first thing that comes off my head.
Yes, I know there’s not a lot left up there, Chris.
Maybe all that’s left now is my last wish.
I used my first wish up asking for world peace,
Hoping to make the world a much better place.
That didn’t work out too well, war increased.
The only peace I see is up in outer space.
I tried again wishing love for everyone,
But the concept was bought and sold by Amazon
And they don’t deliver it to where I’m from
So I’m just left wondering where has it all gone?
I’ve got one left and I don’t want to waste it
Wishing for money or poems that aren’t shit
Or wishing for more hair up there, let’s face it
I can’t change my life by wishing to replace it.

I’m like a pigeon trying to fly in the wind
I’ve got legs stretched and I’m flapping my wings
I’m fighting forces that are stronger than me
Try as I might I’m being swept out to sea.
I’m like a pigeon whose feathers are ruffled
Who’s been through wars and definitely struggled
Flying for home, you might see me hurrying
I’ve lost the message that I once was carrying.
I’m like the pigeons you see in the square
One of thousands of others who still flock there
Begging for titbits you throw on the ground
Taking off in a panic at the slightest sound.
I’m like a pigeon with one beady eye
And one gammy leg so I hop but can’t fly
Scruffy and battled and a bit of a clown
Maybe that’s where the allegory breaks down.

I like to think there’s a poem somewhere
Filled with all the words I’ve deleted from here
They didn’t sit right in the piece I was writing
But now they have found a work more exciting.
I don’t like to think of them lurking in limbo
When they could club together and go to a disco
Get all jumbled up and have new word babies
Create a new genre, called ‘orphapoems’ maybe?
So long as they’re not just trapped in the dark
In the equivalent of an abandoned car park
Growing delinquent and playing with guns
Steeling the metaphors when I send new ones.
No, I hope that they’re happy wherever they are
Because misplaced words can cause so much harm.

I find myself stranded, hung by a thread
Heart-worn to a nub by my own lack
Confronted by the very wight I dread
A creature I have carried on my back.
As shepherd I can contemplate the loom
It’s form if not the workings of the beast
Yet in my heart I know it spells my doom
Its creations will swaddle me at least.
Mocked am I, by college studied texts
That echo my despair as readers weep.
Fair devoid of meaning, shadows flex
I stretch for the light but lie too deep.
For here I delved for truth but had no spade
While Eve spun pure gold into her brocade.

I saw two snails on a tree
Climbing up relentlessly
Their motive was a mystery
Maybe that’s how God sees me?
I don’t climb trees so often now
I don’t seem to remember how
I would though, to the highest bough
If flesh and spirit and God allowed.
I left the snails to their task
Climbing their own Everest
Intervention wasn’t for the best
I hope God saw and was impressed.

The camera club meets
once a week in the church hall
Talk of technique and
show pictures that are beautiful
Swans that are graceful and
buildings that are so tall
And maybe swap a few lenses.
Views of the world are
brought in and dissected
Faces of all kinds
of folk are collected
Interesting angles and
new views projected
and colours that dazzle the senses.
To some members
Proficiency’s all important
For others it’s story
Shown by the content
I feel that beauty
Is born of intent
And out of all this magic condenses.

I can’t write a poem about wind
As it might be misconstrued
And writing about blowing and gusts
Eventually starts to sound rude.
Yet the wind tonight is awfully bad
Shaking the windows and door
And it’s gusting around noisily
It could blow the roof off I’m sure.

And the thought of rhyming makes me nauseous
Times when I’m so fed up with trying to create
That it all feels so pointless, so utterly worthless.
So I sit and smoulder and hate the process
And get distracted, sometimes deliberately
And go out for a walk or anything, anything
But sit down to do something miserably.
Until I finally get to the place where to write
anything would be better than feeling like this
So I stare at the screen and the flashing cursor
And draw out what’s hiding, even if it resists.
Until finally I find I’ve written something like this
It’s not worth much but it kept me from the abyss.

When I feel the internal beat
The drums that call my heart to war
I am drawn to leave my seat and

Skip through the newly opened door.
I shall dance around the garden
And not care for talk or clothes
Visit shrubs as though a parson
Dancing where I am enclosed.
Ride the waves of body rhythms
Oblivious yet so aware
Freed of all my own conditions
Let the stars and heavens stare.
I will dance when all else fails me
To the tempo that doesn’t slow
Leave the flesh and cares that jail me
Travel forth as a twirling soul.

is bank holiday fun
and watching Ben Hur on the telly
Others are egg eaters
Chocolatey self treaters
Some people prefer Figolli.
Some folk are working
Serving or clerking
Saving their treats for later
Some people are praying
A debt they’re repaying
Their minds on something greater.
Some have parties thrown
While some are alone
Eating their own Easter dishes.

Whatever you’re up to
I’m thinking of you
And sending warm Easter wishes.

When spring arrives
it brightens our lives
With friends I love to see
Like dragonflies
and baby mice
and humble bumblebees.
As nature wakes
and yawns and shakes
the shiver from her dresses
Her song calls forth
A rising warmth
And all the earth it blesses.
So I’ll give thanks
For riverbanks
And forests full of life
For morning walks
With noisy squawks
And without winters strife.

I woke up in bed
With a list in my head
Of the things that I needed to buy:
Tissues, milk, and some crisps
Not a very long list
Oh, and also some sort of pie.
Its just a short trip
Through the park if I’m quick
To throw the odd ball for the dog.
But my brain is like cotton
And I realised I’d forgotten
Some of my shopping catalogue.
So I walked down the lane
Wracking my poor brain
For the things that I needed to buy
Something and milk and erm
Something else, and ahhh
Some sort of tasty meat pie.
I came to a stop
Standing outside the shop
Tying the dog to a post out the way.
Perhaps looking inside
The shop would provide
A reverse to my mental decay.
But once in the establishment
I was consumed by bafflement
At the plethora that met my eyes
I bought a bottle of wine
Some cheese that looked fine
And a frisbee for the dog to try.
I walked straight home
Feeling oddly alone
There I remembered my mistake
There were things that I needed
To the shop I stampede
For the dog that I’d left tied by the gate.

Every. Single. Night.
I’m ready for bed
But the cat wants to play
She’s always more feisty
At this time of day.
I’ve hidden the catnip
I’ve not got a treat
This seems to enrage her
She’s attacking my feet.
Then there’s some purring
But it’s just a ruse
She’s planning violence
More toe attack/abuse.
I ought to stop wiggling them
It just winds her up
Then Bam! It’s the zoomies
She’s knocks over my cup.
That seems to spook her
and she’s off down the stairs
To pounce on the dogs
And cause chaos elsewhere.

All the road signs I went hurtling past
I should’ve given more attention
I would’ve missed the dangerous curves
I might have reached my destination
If you had been my map reader
I’d have listened to what you’d say
The warnings that you’d have seen
Said “200 Yards, Give Way”.
I turned the satnav off, trusting
My own sense of direction
I thought I’d been this way before
But life throws out distractions
With the last few miles to go
The clouds above turned grey
I was going far too fast to stop
There were 50 yards to go, give way.
There was the sound of screaming brakes
There was the smell of rubber burnt
There was a blur of coloured shapes
There was a flash of what I’d learnt.
Don’t go too fast you miss the signs
Don’t treat them as a cabaret
Listen to the one you love
And when you must, give way.

I’m whistling wishes as I walk along
Humming my hopes as a huggable song
Puffing out prophecy in improbable places
Fishing for friendliness in favourable faces.
I’m rolling my resources relatively randomly
And halving my helplessness handsomely.
While etching my ease almost elegantly
And giggling at the gibbous gentry.
Why am I so high I should sigh softly?
What wiles have I got that besot so?
This: I am tired of the treadmill
So whistling and humming I will go.

When the night is empty
The star are curtained off
No sounds from the highway
I hesitate to cough.
Critters hiding silently
In the heavy rough
When the night is empty
The silence is enough.
I took a walk along the street
In streetlight blur and shadows
I felt the stillness of the night
The hush upon the meadows
The only walker in the world
The only serene wanderer
Senses straining fruitlessly
A solitary night ponderer
I felt the absence of the waves
That normally crash endlessly
I felt I’d reached a turning point
Received a message soundlessly.
A premise that if followed through
And brought to crystal clarity
Was shattered by approaching cars
and returned reality.
When the night is empty
And you embrace the emptiness
The universe can disappear
and lucidity can coalesce.

There are beings like me
Who hurt themselves deliberately.
I’m not one of them particularly
As I wouldn’t stand the pain
And I’d need them to explain
What do they get out of it, specifically?
Is it expression of some inner mess
Or an urge that they must confess
I’m still confused nonetheless.
It must feel so good yet also bad
Like smuggling illicit contraband
Creating scars more or less.
My scars are on the inside of me
Deep within where none can see
They’re part of my individuality
Some are mine and some are from others
Folks whom I once called friends or lovers
Yet stabbed at me repeatedly.
They too are beings like me
But they are not like me at all.

I drive my old car from A to B
Sometimes I breakdown in-between
It’s got me this far despite it all.
I drove it here and now I will see

If someone will come to tow me
Get me to C but at a slow crawl.
I need a chauffeur and limousine
So I can sip champagne in between
These long interminable ordeals.
I need a satnav or at least some maps
My time driving would be less perhaps
I need to get a new set of wheels.

Life drives a steamroller
Drunk at the controls
Slow but unstoppable
Ever onward it rolls.
I am the traffic cone
That stood in its way
Hollow and comical
Flattened today.

We lie together in our bed
A place where we are one
Two hearts beat beneath the sheets
Our tangled knot undone.
Her gentle breathing calms my heart
Her tiredness is prevailing
I snuggle close so I can feel
Her dreams as she’s exhaling.
I close my eyes and believe
That I can join her there
Sharing that internal space
Where we are both laid bare.

My love sends me a postcard
When she travels abroad
Some short sweet lines of love
With not a wasted word.
When I’m away from her
I send lengthy ardent letters.
But ten thousand words of mine
are wasted. Hers are better.

You’re cast in bronze upon your plinth
Uncaring, solid and imperious
Midas touched and genies wished
Immune to all experience.
I’m cast in shade by your great stature
Waiting for the sun to shift
Shine some light on what is truth
And also on what’s been cast adrift.

My wheels are spinning
As I rush through life
Am I out of control?
I’m not asking twice.
Flying over the ridges
Bottom out in the dips
Grinding gears as I go
Silent prayer on my lips.
My wheels are spinning
As ideas hurtle by
Out of reach out the window
In the wind, on the fly.
0r getting mown down
By the great tyred beast
Swallowed, spat out
Desperate speed is increased.
My wheels are spinning
Like plates in the air
With me underneath them
Keep them up there.
All this combustion
All this carbon expense
Burning rubber and bridges
Defies common sense.

Don’t count sheep, the bleating’s too loud
Don’t read scary stories, you’ll be shaken and cowed.
Don’t pace up and down in your pyjamas
Don’t chew your nails reliving dramas.
Don’t drink coffee or excessive alcohol
Don’t sneak downstairs for a quick bacon roll.
Don’t phone a friend (unless it’s an emergency)
Don’t beat yourself up, literally or internally
Don’t search the web, on your phone, aimlessly
Don’t cry for hours even if it feels necessary.
Don’t question your motives or earlier actions
Don’t do equations with improper fractions
Don’t imagine you’re on a beach under a palm tree
Don’t sit in the dark trying to write poetry.

You don’t have to be sensitive
Or have any special gifts
You don’t have to believe at all
To feel the way the curtain shifts.
If you look almost anywhere
Open your eyes and take it in
You’ll see faces everywhere
Especially where the veil is thin.
Scepticism may be religion
You may doubt just what you see
Doubts may lead to deeper questions
What’s behind the blind is now set free.
They don’t need your recognition
They don’t ask for your permission
They don’t rely on your condition
They’ve chosen to make this transition.

I like to see, that makes it real
But some things I must take on trust
Until we improve methods and
observations are more robust.
I picture you through resonance
And combing through reams of data,
My feelings are in constant flux and
Will need careful research later.
You, as the subject of my study,
Tantalise and fascinate me
I love you on the quantum level
But that is where my learning fails me.
With equations I unravel
The signals you are sending me
Help to plot out the position
Where I can wait on bended knee
The waves and matrices entwine
The way I hope our bodies will
But all the mathematics is
Still sadly far beyond my skill
I have found that the more I learn
Like how you move and operate
Makes me certain that I love you
But less sure you reciprocate.

I close my eyes so I can see
What is right in front of me
But I can’t touch what isn’t there
And I can’t breathe in this fresh air.
I close my eyes so I don’t see
All this deep woe I guarantee
Will drag my soul to hollow home
A torture like I’ve never known.
I close my eyes here in the dark
Close the case then disembark
Leaving tarnished hope behind
To hunt mythical peace of mind.
I’d feed my eyes both to the birds
If I could perhaps unwrite the words
Give my tongue as a second course
To be in darkness and find the source.
Would I then enlightened be?

Make finding it one of your goals.

Like a dream that you’ve lived in before.

Taken for granted yet precious to possess.
Taken for granted yet precious to possess.

Bringing us closer to the source of ourselves
Revealing our innermost feelings.
Revealing our innermost feelings

Oh my dear old mum

I couldn’t think of words to write
So I had to ask someone
They said they’d do it for free
Which was quite alright with me
Because nothing says “I love you Mum”
Like doing things cheaply.
So Mum this is what you’ve got
Three verses, not a lot.

Ezra the catboy can leap so gracefully
He spins in mid air and lands on one knee
Under the stars on a warm Texan night
Dreams of heroes and baddies they’d fight.
Strong, just like the Alamos walls
The catboy withstands all of life’s brawls
Ezras mouth betrays the hint of a smile
Living the movies of the mind in style
Chasing robots through Natural Bridge Caverns

Helping your friends to unravel the patterns
Down Paseo del Rio they fly in pursuit
“They’re getting away, we’ve got to scoot!”
Ezras eyes flicker, did he hear a noise?

The soft Texan wind blows in sleepy kisses
In the dream Catboy pounces but misses

Spiderman swings in and the chase soon ends
Ezra fires webs at all the rogue robots

Your mask and PJ’s tucked under your pillow.

Love can be complicated

Trust in your instincts.
We’ve all got those voices

Love’s sweet, life’s short

I’ve driven down this street a time or two
Winter dripping from lampposts in the mist

Hedges show thorns and empty lonely nest.
People steam head down through wild wind
Dragging dogs or children weighted anchors
The saddest Lowry paintings here distilled
Struggling hard against the seasons rancour
The trees amid the ooze beseech the skies
Last years foliage has long been missing
Then an uplifting sight thrills a weary eye
A cherries early bloom gives hope of spring.

Blocked
Too much
It’s not fun now
I’m struggling
To go on
Don’t want to push
Straining seems wrong
When it should flow
What could flow
You’d be shocked

Lost motivation
To push myself
Who’s it for if not me?

In this now
My inspiration
Has stopped
I’m blocked
I’ve forgotten
The beginning
Lost my way
Ended up here
It’s not the best place
I hide my face
Defy expectations
The pressures
A prison
It can’t be unlocked
So I’m blocked.

What’s in the pot?
What’s bubbling away?
What needs a stir?

You know somethings simmering

You have a quick sample

Turn up the heat
On your best ironware
Mix into the frying pan
What’s been prepared
Plate it all up with
an extravagant flourish
I hope that this serving
Will satisfy and nourish.

The gravel in the riverbed.
I’m deep under water
With folk just like me
Rolling on slowly
On our way to the sea
We started so bold but
Got caught in a landslide
Crashed into a stream
Which became our guide
This journey is long
And it wears us away
Until we’re fine sand
On the beach in the bay.

My heart is bursting.
Love is the question.
I’m yearning and thirsting.
The lasting impression.
Here is my troth!
A horse called devotion.
Loves bubbling broth.
I belong in your ocean.
The search for (unfinished).

Loves gentle progression.
You’re my favourite mammal.
The reason I love you.
Love Bites! (That’s all)
How my heart grew.

Time skips forward every four years

Doing things I now can’t remember

Days lost to illness, tears and pain

Facebook moderators often are

Protecting groups from nipple art

Casual members are the pond birds
These park keepers try to protect
From great offence at careless words
That the bots fail to detect
Oh, that my heart had knights like these
A keep safe from all life’s sharp kicks
Who care about my unknown needs
Fight by my side through loves conflicts.
That I might scroll and post in peace
And my wounded soul may be at ease.

The king of the memes
Is oversharing his wares
Showing himself carelessly
Thoughtless of all he bares.
Queen of the game apps
Is watching some adverts
Topping up her bonus pots
Numbing the stuff that hurts.

Searching then swiping away
Not looking for anything really

The next generation will have something else

Our folks had cigarettes

Enjoy it now before they say
You shouldn’t do that anymore.

Standing in the queue at

Shuffling forward slowly

Everyday is an anniversary

Light shines and shadows fall
On my reluctant rodent.

The galaxy broadcasts to me

We’ve searched for its hidden code
But none’s been found so I am told.
But when I can find a quiet place
Far from the noisy human race

I let my brain absorb the transmission
So my stardust cells get their nutrition.

If you notice I’m gone for a day or two

Ideas simmering under review.

Give it a stir and see what you get
It may be quicker to go to Tibet.
Talk of a watched pot will never do
It takes a while to get me in a stew
So give me some space to do what I do
I will be back once I’ve had me a brew.

I find I’m a bit lost

Am I an autumn?

We’re mad and bad
And dangerous to know
We’re unpredictable
Too fast and too slow.
Wherever we’re invited
We don’t disappoint

We come to the party
And trash the joint.
We’ll fight with your friends
And with each other
We’ll piss in the punchbowl
We’ll upset your mother.
The food will be eaten
We’ll empty the bar
We’ll find drinks you’ve hidden
Wherever they are.
You can’t uninvite us
We’d turn up anyway
You can’t kick us out
We’re here to stay.

Little crab living in a bottle lid
It’s much lighter than old style shells
Is the crab happier in his home
Do the older crabs mock where he dwells?
He’s not so tired with a plastic house
He’s got more energy to mate and grow
Do the youngsters think he’s cool
With this multi-coloured shell show?
Bottle tops thrown into the ocean
Lids left lying on the beach sand
Recycled by the homeless hermits
This evolution was unplanned.

I’m in the dentists chair
Trying to think up some verse
But it’s not very easy when
Aaggggggghhhhhh
Sorry that was unexpected
She must have touched a nerve
Now they’re talking about gums
Mostly ones – uggghhhh gurrve
Am I flossing regularly?
Gurgle gluk gurgle nod

I roll my eyes, receive a prod.
There’s talk of xrays
Crowns and bridges

I’m sent to the hygienist.

My poetry evolution
Began so long ago
As soon as I learnt how to write
I had to have a go.
Preteen me wrote limericks
And poems full of gore
My revenge on bullies
Idle fantasies, no more.
In my teens I changed a bit

My poems turned to songs
To impress the girl next door
I dreamed she’d sing along.
In my twenties I would write
Love songs full of angst
Bemoaning my loneliness
I sat and wrote and drank.
The wailing turned wooing
And the words won me a wife
To my delight I found that love
Gave me a muse for life.
In my thirties kids arrived
Though now it’s quite a blur
My poems became lullabies
The type that kids prefer.
Time went past so full of stuff
That parents have to do
My poet time was given up
And put to other use.
But children grow and I found
A bit of time to spare
And I discovered deep inside
The poems were still there.
I’ve been through the larval stage
And caterpillars crawl
I’ve been locked in my cocoon
And broken through the wall.
Now my metaphors will rise
Like some ungodly insect
And cough up all the poetry

That time let me collect.
As years pass I’ll add to this
Another verse or five
And see if my evolution
Continues till I die.

I find it hard to write from the heart,

Reliving pain poetically is

I want to bring the feelings out
To scorn my sadly injured soul,
It is a struggle every day
To fight against a poets goal.
Forgive me for my poor attempt
To expose my weaknesses here,
I fear that for now they’ve won the day
So I must just persevere.

A haunting cry from the dark

A figure appears

A scream but cut short

All quiet again.

That someone else checks
If there is some therapy
That would be great
So long as its scheduled
And on the right date.

Start tugging at my
Unconscious depression

Take a few moments

Looking back where I was
At my long journey here
Looking ahead at
The road through the years.

And life is the journey

Why are cupboards called cupboards
Are the cups just lodging there?

Do sideboards rent space to sides?
Cabinets put me in mind of
Tiny rooms on sailing ships
How did they end up instead
On bathroom walls affixed?
Wardrobes too leave me confused
Are robes wards when they are used?
Do we unleash the drobes of war
When we leave clothes upon the floor?
But there’s a sense of mystery
To how those titles were gained
I doubt folk will wonder much
How washing machines were named.

Tonight I’m feeling winters chilly grip
I’m watching where I walk in case I slip
Feeling frozen grass crack beneath my feet
Sniffing frigid air for signs of snow or sleet.
Tonight my precious breath is clear to me
Hanging drifty in the air for all to see
Mingling with strangers clouds as they pass
Forming rivers on the cafés misted glass.
Tonight the streetlights can not dim the stars
Through crystal air they twinkle down on frosted cars
And the cities distinctive scent is mixed with winter
Cleaner, clearer, though mixed with chimneys cinder
Tonight the cold is king of this domain
And we must dash or feel it in our frame
As time takes us further from the sun
We hoard warmth and wait for spring to come.

When I’m doing the washing I sometime feel
That the washing I’m doing is somewhat like me.
This t-shirt for example has seen better days
It’s picture has faded and it’s turned a bit grey.
These trouser are baggy but once were well fitted
To higher class venues they’d not be admitted.
My shirt collars that were starched stiff and white
Are off-colour and limp, and do not excite.
My Jumpers have bobbles and fuzz in the knit
They’ve shrunk somehow and don’t quite fit.
The pile of old socks that don’t properly match
Are worn at the heals and cause me to scratch.
I bundle them all in on a quick all-purpose cycle
Like some deranged washing mad psycho
Knowing they’ll come out all horribly wrinkled
And like the t-towels my edges will be crinkled.

There are two files on my computer
The books of joy and darkness
My words fill both of them
And yet they are both ravenous.
I feed them from my very soul
They drink my blood, sweat and tears
One day there will be nothing left
And that’s my greatest fear.
Both I find unbearable
To me they are so well known
Both books contain parts of me
That I have never shown.
The book of joy burns so bright
All else is cast in shadow
It is the me I wish to be
The me I’ll seldom know.
The book of darkness also burns
As redheads do when blushing.
It’s where I writhe in anguish
As my weaknesses come gushing.
I keep them on my old PC
Encrypted and protected
Here they keep me virus free
Though bad sectors are detected.

Welcome to the year of peace
When fighting of all kinds will cease
Humankind will live as one
On this rock we live upon
There’s no room for war no more
So no one now needs to keep score
Although we don’t all get along
We’re family so we all belong
Think of all the money saved
The folk who won’t have early graves
The building we can do, instead
Of turning these green fields red
We’re better off without our guns
Except for some essential ones
To remind us in the future
Just how stupid you and I were
Let’s spend this year fixing bridges
Instead of threats let’s send kisses
And as the year goes by we’ll find
Our mental health needs peace of mind.

I like snoozing by the fire

I like snoring in the hallway
While the puppies are at play
I like sleeping by the bed
Dreaming of meals I’ve had

If I find one on the floor
I can snaffle sneaky biscuits

I can hoover up your dinner
Though you’ll say that I am bad

I’ll go barking mad!
I will consent to go for walkies
To do the business that I need.
I will run across a field
If you take me off the lead
I will come back home smelling
Of the thing in which I rolled
But if I meet the postman

Eighteen years since becoming a parent

Drying the tears and finding new strength
Solving frustrations, experiencing thrills.

You have helped me to grow and develop
I was an unopened flower needing sun.
Eighteen years to get to this point
The start of a new chapter begins
Sure to be full of your special magic
That distills the joy parenting brings.

I had an idea for a poem

But when I sat down to write it
I found I was poem blind.
The words in my head were clear
But the ones I wrote out were a mess
I couldn’t keep to the theme and

Find solace in coffee or chocolate

Before long I have a collection

That someday I may try to salvage
Or spin into gold perhaps.
In this dark greenhouse they’ll lurk in the gloom
Until I feed them and wait for their bloom.

I have a selection of single socks
All sadly separated from their mates

And a few of them go out on dates.
They once all had perfect sock partners
But time always takes its harsh toll
Some fell apart, some got eaten by dogs
One was turned into a doll.
Those that remain sit forlornly
Missing the ones that have gone
Wondering if there’s another
That’s out there waiting to be worn.
They meet on my bed for a mingle
And some of them find a new friend
Someone who’ll do for a day or two
But who’ll get lost in the wash in the end.

Odd days and feast days
Are spread through the year
Adding some spice to our lives

You celebrate yours
And I’ll celebrate mine
That way both of us thrives.
Odd ways, peculiarities
We’ve all got our share
Of foibles that others find strange
I won’t judge yours
If you’ll just ignore mine
There’s nothing we need to change.
Off days and maladies
They come to us all
Some much more than others
I’ll be there for yours
Because you’re there for me
We’re stronger helping one another.

When I can’t think clearly
I think of the past
Of our love and how
The time moved so fast.
Tracing our journey
From steam to river
To the wild open ocean
Where we’ll sail forever.
When the mists on my mind
Like the clouds on the hill
I think of our hearts
And the joy they distill.
If the fog ever clears
And the sun can shine
Light up our valley
With a warmth so divine.
When I’m in darkness
I see your golden hair
And that fills up my lungs
Like the fresh mountain air.
Sometimes a hurricane
At others a breeze
Our love fills the sails
As we cross these wide seas.

Despite the coat and hat and gloves
The wind stabs cold at my face.
We reach a style, I’m over, they’re under.
Away in the distance there’s a rumble of thunder.
Tonight the darkness on the field seems threatening
Orion in the sky is unwelcoming
But I’ve no choices remaining
The irrevocable future is beckoning
Unwashed destiny is strangling
Any hope I have of escaping.
Another flash and I see them start
Bright collars against the dark
Immune to the threat in the air
Uncaring of my diminished spark.

Imagine having nothing to do
Except whatever you wanted to do.
That could be nothing, nothing at all
Or it could be whatever you want.
You could sit and exist quietly
Pondering existence itself
Contemplating your reason for sitting
But not needing to find relief.
Letting those moments go by
Oblivious to the way that time flies
Denying the needs of the moment
Ignoring what others may want.
Imagine having time off
No need to worry or stress
Or cook the food or pay the bills
Or have anything left to possess.
Sometimes that which we desperately need
Is what stops us and scares us indeed.

There’s a library I’ve built in my mind
Where I’m never quite sure what I’ll find.
All the books I collected and fastidiously read,
The words transferred from the page to my head,
Where they tumble and rumble and make quite a mess,
They bounce off the walls and the thoughts I’ve suppressed.
There’s a quiet place hidden there in the storm
Where my own words can falteringly form.
I try to catch them and sometimes I do
And occasionally there’s something shiny and new,
But mostly it’s something like this
That I’ll pin down on paper and then dismiss.

The day after Christmas
Must be Christmas for cats,
With all the new places
They can hide, bite and scratch.
All the unboxed surprises
Now cherished lovingly,
While their empty containers
Are discarded thoughtlessly.
Piled near the back door
To be taken to the bin,
But beware when you do
A cat might be within.
They’re perfect to climb on,
Dark and secret inside,
Sometimes full of Styrofoam
And much more beside.
Is there a cat in there?
Only Schrodinger knows
If it‘s possibly snuffed it
Or its just having a nose.
In the perfect place
To plan a kitty attack
On the poor foolish person
Who tries to take one back.

How long does it take to fly right round the world?
I guess it depends on your speed.
How do you harness a magic reindeer
So you’ll move fast enough to succeed?
How many presents can fit in your sack?
How do you sort them all out?
Is there a roster of where to go when
Or an elf that you can’t do without?
Does an open top sleigh get cold as you fly
Or does your high speed create friction?
Does your fir lined suit have an adjustable waist
To cope with your mince pie addiction?
How much love does it take to care that all
The good kids of the world gets a visit?
Do you take a packed lunch to eat on your way,
That replenishes your Christmas spirit?
Do you think of past years as you fly merrily,
All the changes in presents delivered?
Do you still feel the joy that gift giving gives?
How we treasure your annual visit!

It’s Christmas shopping eve
And I’m dreading hitting the shops
I should have gone online
And ordered everybody socks.
The car parks are going to be rammed
And everyone will be in a rush,
Browsing for gifts in a haberdashers
Should I buy them a new toilet brush?
Squeezed down aisles in the supermarket,
The shelves either stuffed with figs,

Or empty of what it was that you need,
So granddad gets chocolatey twigs.
Dash past the buskers and donut stand,
Dance past the carolling choir,
Prance through the German Market stalls,
Commit to a new washer-dryer.
Maybe in all of the bustle,
I’ll come across some Christmas cheer,
Maybe a free mince pie or two,
Or the reason why we’re all here.
Maybe take a moment to enjoy it,
All the bright seasonal colours
All the folk dashing from shop to shop,
Buying gifts for their significant others.

And she was his shadow,
Tears were about to fall as the Creator ordered him to fly back...
As a mere mortal felt in love with the an angel,

Her last wish was to lift her life along to his flight...
But the sins of her heart has slaved her soul to this world,

She felt asleep...
When his wings were waving the freshness of heaven to comb her hair,

Moons later...
She gave life to a little light,

Alone she prayed for a reunion...
Separation of a lifetime would lead to the eternal bond.

The clouds undressed the moon with the wind...
The heartbreak kid was roaming on the frozen lake,

The thin ice began to crack...
And the broken heart was aspired into another world,

The secret garden of dreams was a reality,
And while walking towards the source of water...
The heart of the garden was a fountain,

A fountain of tears perfumed by petals of rose...
At last he found a place where to seek refuge,

His soul refreshed while tasting the water...
An angel flew the bird back from the eternal garden,

When he woke up...
He realised that nature was heaven on earth.

Friend to sadness,
The wind curling her hair between my fingers...
A dream meant to remain untold in this reality,

The arrow transpierced the flesh...
And the heart could have harden with pain,

Tears burning my eyes...
The heart melted the arrow,

Since the creation of time...

When next love turns the knob of my door,
I’ll check its credentials.
The last time it showed up,
love tried surgery without a license.
It stepped into the OR of my heart,
scrubbed in like it knew every procedure,
like the anatomy was memorized,
like my chambers were open textbooks.
My heart was fractured,
ripped in places I didn’t even know existed.
I signed the consent form,
laid down quietly,
hoping on the anesthesia of trust.
I watched as it fumbled instruments,
scalpel trembling in untrained hands,
hesitating at the wrong arteries,
cutting deeper into fragile walls,
missing the signs that screamed for care.
I should have called off the surgery,
but the anesthesia numbed my fear
and my caution.
I watched it leave incisions where trust once sat,
tear at sutures that were only half-formed,
stitch wounds haphazardly,
pulling threads too tight,

tearing tissue already raw,
and called it care.
I felt the cold steel of unskilled hands,
the weight of intent without skill,
the silent chaos of a heart left open,
exposed to missteps,
to pauses, to fear.
So when next love drives by,
I hope it’s a certified surgeon
one who knows my heart’s anatomy.
I hope it wears gloves of patience,
wields instruments with knowledge,
and knows that each cut must be deliberate.
I hope it traces every bruise,
sews every scar with intention,
and listens to the rhythm before acting.
I hope love scrubs in fully trained.
I refuse to bleed under unskilled hands again.

before it becomes arrest.

without breaking ribs,

when the heart resists returning.

follows the trauma back
to its origin,

not just the symptoms.

Beauty in the Soul
Beauty lives in her pulse,

steady, defiant.
In the way she rises after breaking,
in the way her laughter survives storms,
in the way her scars refuse erasure.
Beauty is the fire that keeps burning
even when no one gathers for warmth.
It is the river that flows
whether or not someone stops to admire it.
It is the sun
never asking the earth
if it deserves to rise.
Some will see it.
Some will miss it.
Some will call it ordinary

because it does not beg.
But beauty was never meant
to kneel before beholders.
It was meant to exist
wild, whole, uncontained.
If only they knew
beauty does not live in the eyes that look
it lives in the soul that dares to be.
If only...

They say beauty is in the eyes of the beholder,

as if worth needs permission,
as if radiance must wait
to be chosen by a gaze.
As if her existence is an audition,
and the world sits in judgment,
thumbs up, thumbs down,
deciding who is allowed to shine.
But whose eyes?
The tired ones trained by magazines?
The wandering ones taught to worship symmetry?
The blind ones that mistake loud for lovely
and silence for nothing?
She has stood before mirrors
that told her lies in fluent reflections.
Mirrors that measured her against standards
manufactured, exported, and enforced.
Mirrors that forgot
they were only glass

not truth.
They told her:
too dark, too soft, too sharp, too much,
not enough.
They cropped her essence
until she almost believed
she was unfinished.
But beauty is not a vote.
It is not a rumor passed from eye to eye.
It is not fragile enough
to die in the absence of applause.

speak louder than the mouths that accuse.

his slow steps,

the finish line keeps moving.

while the world counts their shadows
and calls it stillness.

The roots she planted

If only she knew

more than a cage,
more than a role.

If only...

And now I sit here, breathing, alive,
Knowing I survived what tried to deprive,
Me of hope, of belonging, of a reason to stay,
I’m still here, still healing, still finding my way.

But because real love knows when not to stay there,
And with all of my heart, as I set you free,
I wish you the happiness that couldn’t be with me.
